## Transform Pipeline System

The transform pipeline system provides a modular framework for data processing through the `Transform` base class and composition utilities. Each transform is a self-contained operation that can be chained together to create complex processing pipelines.

### Core Transform Classes

| Transform Class | Purpose | Key Methods |
|---|---|---|
| `Transform` | Abstract base class for all transforms | `forward()`, `check_input()` |
| `Compose` | Chains multiple transforms sequentially | `__call__()` |
| `ConditionalRoute` | Routes data based on conditions | `condition_func` parameter |
| `RandomRoute` | Stochastic routing between transforms | `probs` parameter |
| `Identity` | Pass-through transform | No-op operation |

### Key Data Processing Transforms

The system includes specialized transforms for different aspects of biomolecular data processing:

**Structural Transforms:**
- `RemoveHydrogens` - Removes hydrogen atoms from structures
- `AtomizeByCCDName` - Converts residues to individual atoms based on CCD codes
- `CropSpatialLikeAF3` - Spatial cropping around regions of interest
- `CropContiguousLikeAF3` - Contiguous sequence cropping

**Encoding Transforms:**
- `EncodeAtomArray` - Converts `AtomArray` to encoded tensors
- `EncodeAF3TokenLevelFeatures` - AF3-specific token encoding
- `EncodeMSA` - Multiple sequence alignment encoding

**Feature Engineering Transforms:**
- `AddAtomFrames` - Computes local coordinate frames
- `AddAF3ChiralFeatures` - Chirality information for AF3
- `AddRF2AABondFeaturesMatrix` - Bond connectivity features

**Sources:** [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/base.py:20-200](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/encoding.py:300-400](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/atom_array.py:1-50]()

## Token Encoding System

The token encoding system converts molecular structures into fixed-length representations suitable for transformer-based models. The system supports both residue-level and atom-level tokenization.

### TokenEncoding Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "TokenEncoding Class"
        A1["token_atoms: dict[str, np.ndarray]"]
        A2["chemcomp_type_to_unknown: dict"]
        A3["token_to_idx: dict"]
        A4["atom_to_idx: dict"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Encoding Types"
        B1["AF2_ATOM14_ENCODING"]
        B2["AF2_ATOM37_ENCODING"] 
        B3["RF2AA_ATOM36_ENCODING"]
        B4["AF3SequenceEncoding"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Token Resolution"
        C1["resolve_unknown_token_name()"]
        C2["UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_TOKEN = 0"]
        C3["chemcomp_type mapping"]
    end
    
    A1 --> C1
    A2 --> C1
    A3 --> B1
    A3 --> B2
    A3 --> B3
    A3 --> B4
    
    C1 --> C2
    C1 --> C3
```

### Standard Encodings

The system provides several pre-defined encodings for popular model architectures:

| Encoding | Atoms per Token | Use Case | Special Features |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AF2_ATOM14_ENCODING` | 14 | AlphaFold2 protein models | Standard amino acids only |
| `AF2_ATOM37_ENCODING` | 37 | AlphaFold2 with extended atoms | Includes OXT terminal atom |
| `RF2AA_ATOM36_ENCODING` | 36 | RoseTTAFold All-Atom | Multi-modal (protein/DNA/RNA/atoms) |
| `AF3SequenceEncoding` | Variable | AlphaFold3 sequence encoding | Hierarchical token structure |

### Token Type Handling

The encoding system distinguishes between different token types:

**Residue-level tokens:** Standard 3-letter CCD codes (e.g., "ALA", "GLY", "DA", "C")
**Atom-level tokens:** Atomic numbers as integers (e.g., 6 for Carbon, 7 for Nitrogen)
**Special tokens:** Masked tokens using angle bracket syntax (e.g., "<M>", "<G>")

**Sources:** [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:36-251](), [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:254-332](), [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:422-520]()

### Pipeline Configuration

Both pipelines support extensive configuration through parameters:

**Common Parameters:**
- `protein_msa_dirs` / `rna_msa_dirs` - MSA directory configurations
- `crop_size` - Maximum tokens in cropped structures  
- `n_recycles` - Number of model recycles during training
- `template_lookup_path` / `template_base_dir` - Template structure paths

**AF3-Specific Parameters:**
- `diffusion_batch_size` - Batch size for diffusion noising
- `sigma_data` - Diffusion noise scaling parameter
- `conformer_generation_timeout` - Timeout for ligand conformer generation

**RF2AA-Specific Parameters:**
- `max_automorphs` / `max_isomorphs` - Symmetry resolution limits
- `black_hole_init` - Initialization strategy
- `unclamp_loss_probability` - Training loss unclamping

**Sources:** [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py:84-403](), [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py:154-350]()

## Dataset Management

The dataset management system provides flexible data loading and preprocessing capabilities through wrapper classes and parsers.

### Dataset Wrapper Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Core Dataset Classes"
        A1["PandasDataset"]
        A2["StructuralDatasetWrapper"] 
        A3["ConcatDatasetWithID"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Dataset Parsers"
        B1["PNUnitsDFParser"]
        B2["InterfacesDFParser"]
        B3["ValidationDFParserLikeAF3"]
        B4["GenericDFParser"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Sources"
        C1["Parquet metadata files"]
        C2["CIF structure files"]
        C3["Chain info annotations"]
        C4["Filter expressions"]
    end
    
    A2 --> A1
    A2 --> B1
    A2 --> B2
    A2 --> B3
    A2 --> B4
    
    B1 --> C1
    B2 --> C1
    B3 --> C1
    B4 --> C2
    
    C1 --> C3
    C1 --> C4
```

### Key Dataset Components

**PandasDataset:** Base dataset class that loads tabular metadata and applies filters
- `data`: DataFrame with example metadata
- `id_column`: Column name for unique example identifiers  
- `filters`: List of pandas query expressions for data filtering
- `columns_to_load`: Subset of columns to load (memory optimization)

**StructuralDatasetWrapper:** Combines tabular metadata with structural data loading
- `dataset`: Underlying `PandasDataset` instance
- `dataset_parser`: Parser for converting metadata to file paths
- `transform`: Transform pipeline to apply to loaded structures
- `cif_parser_args`: Arguments passed to CIF file parsing

**Dataset Parsers:** Convert metadata rows to structure file paths and parsing arguments
- `PNUnitsDFParser`: Extracts individual polymer-non-polymer units
- `InterfacesDFParser`: Handles protein-protein/protein-nucleic interfaces
- `ValidationDFParserLikeAF3`: Formats validation datasets for AF3-style evaluation

### Usage Example

The system supports complex dataset composition and filtering:

```python
# Create base dataset with filtering
pn_units_dataset = PandasDataset(
    data=metadata_df,
    id_column="example_id", 
    filters=[
        "deposition_date < '2022-01-01'",
        "resolution < 5.0",
        "num_polymer_pn_units <= 20"
    ]
)

# Wrap with structural processing
structural_dataset = StructuralDatasetWrapper(
    dataset=pn_units_dataset,
    dataset_parser=PNUnitsDFParser(),
    transform=build_af3_transform_pipeline(...),
    cif_parser_args={"cache_dir": None}
)
```

**Sources:** [src/atomworks/ml/datasets/datasets.py](), [src/atomworks/ml/datasets/parsers/](), [tests/ml/conftest.py:167-244]()

### MSA Configuration

MSA directories are configured as lists of dictionaries specifying search paths:

```python
protein_msa_dirs = [
    {
        "dir": "/path/to/protein/msas",
        "extension": ".a3m.gz", 
        "directory_depth": 2
    }
]

rna_msa_dirs = [
    {
        "dir": "/path/to/rna/msas",
        "extension": ".afa",
        "directory_depth": 0  
    }
]
```

### Template Structure Format

The `RF2AATemplate` dataclass encapsulates template information:
- `xyz`: Template coordinates `[1, n_templates × n_atoms, 14, 3]`
- `mask`: Atom presence mask `[1, n_templates × n_atoms, 14]` 
- `qmap`: Query-template alignment mapping `[1, n_templates × n_atoms, 2]`
- `f0d`: Template metadata including sequence similarity `[1, n_templates, 8]`
- `seq`: Template sequence tokens `[1, n_templates × n_atoms]`
- `ids`: Template PDB and chain identifiers

**Sources:** [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/msa/msa.py:1-100](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/template.py:42-213](), [tests/ml/transforms/msa/test_featurize_msa.py:46-120]()

# Page: Transform Pipeline

# Transform Pipeline

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py](src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py)
- [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py](src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py)
- [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/encoding.py](src/atomworks/ml/transforms/encoding.py)
- [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/template.py](src/atomworks/ml/transforms/template.py)
- [tests/io/components/test_regression.py](tests/io/components/test_regression.py)
- [tests/io/tools/test_rdkit.py](tests/io/tools/test_rdkit.py)
- [tests/ml/conftest.py](tests/ml/conftest.py)
- [tests/ml/transforms/msa/test_featurize_msa.py](tests/ml/transforms/msa/test_featurize_msa.py)
- [tests/ml/utils/test_io.py](tests/ml/utils/test_io.py)

</details>



The Transform Pipeline is the core data processing system in atomworks.ml that converts molecular structures into machine learning-ready features through modular, composable transformations. This system provides a unified framework for preprocessing AtomArray objects into model-specific input formats for deep learning models like AlphaFold 3 and RoseTTAFold 2 All-Atom.

For information about the underlying data representation, see [Core Parser System](#2.1). For details about specific model pipelines, see [Model-Specific Pipelines](#3.3).

## System Architecture

The transform pipeline follows a functional composition pattern where individual transforms are chained together to create complete preprocessing workflows. Each transform operates on a data dictionary containing an `AtomArray` and associated metadata, progressively adding features and annotations.

### Core Transform Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Transform Base System"
        A[Transform] --> B[Compose]
        A --> C[ConditionalRoute]
        A --> D[RandomRoute]
        A --> E[ApplyFunction]
        A --> F[Identity]
    end
    
    subgraph "Transform Categories"
        G["Encoding<br/>EncodeAtomArray<br/>EncodeAF3TokenLevelFeatures"]
        H["Filtering<br/>RemoveHydrogens<br/>HandleUndesiredResTokens"]
        I["Atomization<br/>AtomizeByCCDName<br/>FlagNonPolymersForAtomization"]
        J["MSA Processing<br/>LoadPolymerMSAs<br/>FeaturizeMSALikeAF3"]
        K["Templates<br/>AddRFTemplates<br/>FeaturizeTemplatesLikeAF3"]
        L["Features<br/>AddAF3ChiralFeatures<br/>AddAtomFrames"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Pipeline Builders"
        M["build_af3_transform_pipeline()"]
        N["build_rf2aa_transform_pipeline()"]
    end
    
    B --> G
    B --> H  
    B --> I
    B --> J
    B --> K
    B --> L
    
    M --> B
    N --> B
    
    subgraph "Data Flow"
        O["AtomArray + metadata"] --> P["Transform Pipeline"] --> Q["Model Features"]
    end
    
    P --> B
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/base.py:26-35](), [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py:84-403](), [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py:154-475]()

## Core Transform System

### Transform Base Class

The `Transform` abstract base class defines the interface for all data transformations. Each transform implements a `forward()` method that takes and returns a data dictionary:

```python
def forward(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]
```

Key base transforms include:
- `Transform` - Abstract base class requiring `forward()` implementation
- `Compose` - Chains multiple transforms sequentially  
- `ConditionalRoute` - Branches execution based on data conditions
- `RandomRoute` - Randomly selects between transform options
- `Identity` - Pass-through transform for conditional logic

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/base.py:26-35]()

### Transform Composition

The `Compose` transform chains multiple transforms together, with optional RNG state tracking for reproducible random operations:

### Transform Composition Flow

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Input Data"] --> B["Transform 1"]
    B --> C["Transform 2"] 
    C --> D["Transform 3"]
    D --> E["..."]
    E --> F["Transform N"]
    F --> G["Output Data"]
    
    subgraph "Compose Logic"
        H["track_rng_state"] --> I["Seed Management"]
        J["Error Handling"] --> K["Transform Validation"]
    end
    
    B -.-> H
    C -.-> H
    D -.-> H
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/base.py:26-35]()

## Model-Specific Pipeline Builders

### AF3 Transform Pipeline

The `build_af3_transform_pipeline()` function creates a comprehensive preprocessing pipeline for AlphaFold 3 models. The pipeline includes data cleaning, tokenization, MSA processing, template handling, and diffusion preparation:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "AF3 Pipeline Stages"
        A["Data Preparation<br/>RemoveHydrogens<br/>FilterToSpecifiedPNUnits<br/>HandleUndesiredResTokens"]
        
        B["Atomization<br/>AtomizeByCCDName<br/>FlagNonPolymersForAtomization"]
        
        C["Cropping<br/>CropContiguousLikeAF3<br/>CropSpatialLikeAF3<br/>RandomRoute"]
        
        D["Feature Engineering<br/>EncodeAF3TokenLevelFeatures<br/>GetAF3ReferenceMoleculeFeatures"]
        
        E["MSA Processing<br/>LoadPolymerMSAs<br/>FeaturizeMSALikeAF3"]
        
        F["Template Processing<br/>AddRFTemplates<br/>FeaturizeTemplatesLikeAF3"]
        
        G["Diffusion Preparation<br/>BatchStructuresForDiffusionNoising<br/>SampleEDMNoise"]
    end
    
    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    
    subgraph "Configuration Parameters"
        H["crop_size: 384<br/>n_recycles: 5<br/>diffusion_batch_size: 48"]
    end
    
    H -.-> C
    H -.-> E
    H -.-> G
```

Key parameters include:
- `crop_size` - Maximum number of tokens after spatial/contiguous cropping
- `n_recycles` - Number of model recycles for MSA processing  
- `diffusion_batch_size` - Batch size for diffusion noise sampling
- `template_lookup_path` - Path to template database
- `protein_msa_dirs`/`rna_msa_dirs` - MSA search directories

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py:84-403]()

### RF2AA Transform Pipeline  

The `build_rf2aa_transform_pipeline()` function creates preprocessing for RoseTTAFold 2 All-Atom models, with additional symmetry handling and different feature aggregation:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "RF2AA Pipeline Stages"
        A["Structure Preparation<br/>RemoveHydrogens<br/>RemoveUnsupportedChainTypes<br/>AddProteinTerminiAnnotation"]
        
        B["Atomization & Sorting<br/>AtomizeByCCDName<br/>SortLikeRF2AA<br/>AddOpenBabelMoleculesForAtomizedMolecules"]
        
        C["Encoding<br/>EncodeAtomArray<br/>RF2AA_ATOM36_ENCODING"]
        
        D["MSA & Templates<br/>LoadPolymerMSAs<br/>FeaturizeMSALikeRF2AA<br/>FeaturizeTemplatesLikeRF2AA"]
        
        E["Bond Features<br/>AddRF2AABondFeaturesMatrix<br/>AddRF2AATraversalDistanceMatrix"]
        
        F["Symmetry<br/>CreateSymmetryCopyAxisLikeRF2AA<br/>max_automorphs/max_isomorphs"]
        
        G["Final Aggregation<br/>AggregateFeaturesLikeRF2AA<br/>RF2AAInputs conversion"]
    end
    
    A --> B
    B --> C  
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
```

RF2AA-specific features:
- `SortLikeRF2AA` - Orders polymer tokens before non-polymer tokens
- `CreateSymmetryCopyAxisLikeRF2AA` - Handles molecular symmetries  
- `AggregateFeaturesLikeRF2AA` - Packages features into `RF2AAInputs` format
- OpenBabel integration for chiral center detection

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py:154-475]()

## Transform Categories

### Encoding Transforms

Encoding transforms convert AtomArray objects into numerical representations suitable for machine learning models:

- `EncodeAtomArray` - Converts coordinates and sequences to token-based encodings
- `EncodeAF3TokenLevelFeatures` - Generates AF3-specific token features  
- `AddTokenAnnotation` - Adds token-level annotations for debugging

The encoding process maps residues and atoms to fixed-size tensors based on `TokenEncoding` definitions.

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/encoding.py:299-400]()

### Filtering Transforms

Filtering transforms clean and validate molecular structures:

- `RemoveHydrogens` - Removes hydrogen atoms for efficiency
- `HandleUndesiredResTokens` - Filters unwanted residue types
- `RemoveUnresolvedPNUnits` - Removes unresolved polymer units
- `FilterToSpecifiedPNUnits` - Keeps only specified structural units

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/filters.py]()

### MSA Processing Transforms

MSA (Multiple Sequence Alignment) transforms handle evolutionary information:

- `LoadPolymerMSAs` - Loads MSA files from disk based on sequence hashes
- `PairAndMergePolymerMSAs` - Merges MSAs across multiple chains
- `FeaturizeMSALikeAF3`/`FeaturizeMSALikeRF2AA` - Creates model-specific MSA features
- `EncodeMSA` - Converts MSA sequences to token indices

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/msa/msa.py]()

### Template Processing

Template transforms incorporate structural templates:

- `AddRFTemplates` - Loads structural templates from database
- `FeaturizeTemplatesLikeAF3` - Creates AF3-compatible template features
- `RandomSubsampleTemplates` - Randomly selects subset of templates

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/template.py:305-460]()

## Configuration and Usage

### Conditional Execution

The pipeline supports conditional execution based on runtime parameters:

```python
ConditionalRoute(
    condition_func=lambda data: data.get("is_inference", False),
    transform_map={
        True: Identity(),          # Skip cropping during inference
        False: cropping_transform  # Apply cropping during training
    }
)
```

### Random Transforms

Random selection between transform options with specified probabilities:

```python
RandomRoute(
    transforms=[
        CropContiguousLikeAF3(crop_size=384),
        CropSpatialLikeAF3(crop_size=384)
    ],
    probs=[0.5, 0.5]  # Equal probability
)
```

### Pipeline Integration

Transform pipelines integrate with dataset wrappers for end-to-end processing:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["PandasDataset"] --> B["StructuralDatasetWrapper"]
    B --> C["DatasetParser"]
    B --> D["Transform Pipeline"]
    C --> E["AtomArray"]
    D --> F["Model Features"]
    E --> D
```

Sources: [tests/ml/conftest.py:300-365](), [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py:84-403](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/base.py:26-35]()

# Page: Token Encodings

# Token Encodings

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yaml](.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yaml)
- [.gitignore](.gitignore)
- [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml)
- [src/atomworks/io/utils/ccd.py](src/atomworks/io/utils/ccd.py)
- [src/atomworks/io/utils/sequence.py](src/atomworks/io/utils/sequence.py)
- [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py](src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py)
- [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/msa/_msa_constants.py](src/atomworks/ml/transforms/msa/_msa_constants.py)
- [tests/io/utils/test_sequence_maps.py](tests/io/utils/test_sequence_maps.py)
- [tests/io/utils/test_sequence_utils.py](tests/io/utils/test_sequence_utils.py)

</details>



This document covers the token encoding system in AtomWorks, which converts molecular sequences and structures into numerical representations suitable for machine learning models. The system provides standardized encodings for different foundation models like AlphaFold 2, AlphaFold 3, and RoseTTAFold 2 All-Atom.

For information about the broader ML transform pipeline that uses these encodings, see [Transform Pipeline](#3.1). For model-specific pipeline implementations, see [Model-Specific Pipelines](#3.3).

## System Overview

The token encoding system bridges the gap between biological sequence representations (1-letter codes, 3-letter codes, atom names) and the numerical tensors required by ML models. It handles both residue-level tokenization (e.g., "ALA" → integer) and atom-level tokenization within residues (e.g., "CA" atom within "ALA" → position index).

## Token Encoding Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Representations"
        A1["`One-letter codes
        A, R, N, D, C, ...`"]
        A2["`Three-letter codes
        ALA, ARG, ASN, ASP, CYS, ...`"]
        A3["`Atom names
        N, CA, C, O, CB, ...`"]
        A4["`Chemical Component Dictionary
        CCD codes and metadata`"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Token Encoding System"
        B1["TokenEncoding class"]
        B2["`token_atoms mapping
        residue → atom positions`"]
        B3["`chemcomp_type_to_unknown
        unknown residue handling`"]
        B4["`resolve_unknown_token_name()
        fallback resolution`"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Predefined Encodings"
        C1["AF2_ATOM14_ENCODING"]
        C2["AF2_ATOM37_ENCODING"] 
        C3["RF2_ATOM14_ENCODING"]
        C4["RF2_ATOM23_ENCODING"]
        C5["RF2_ATOM36_ENCODING"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Sequence Utilities"
        D1["`get_1_from_3_letter_code()
        3-letter → 1-letter`"]
        D2["`get_3_from_1_letter_code()
        1-letter → 3-letter`"]
        D3["`aa_chem_comp_3to1()
        amino acid mappings`"]
        D4["`na_chem_comp_3to1()
        nucleic acid mappings`"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Tensors"
        E1["`Token indices
        [0, 1, 2, 3, ...]`"]
        E2["`Atom indices
        [0, 1, 2, 3, ..., 13]`"]
        E3["`Element types
        [N, C, C, O, C, ...]`"]
        E4["`Coordinate masks
        [1, 1, 1, 1, 0, ...]`"]
    end
    
    A1 --> D1
    A2 --> D2
    A3 --> B2
    A4 --> B3
    
    D1 --> B1
    D2 --> B1
    B2 --> B1
    B3 --> B1
    B4 --> B1
    
    B1 --> C1
    B1 --> C2
    B1 --> C3
    B1 --> C4
    B1 --> C5
    
    C1 --> E1
    C2 --> E1
    C3 --> E1
    C4 --> E1
    C5 --> E1
    
    C1 --> E2
    C2 --> E2
    C3 --> E2
    C4 --> E2
    C5 --> E2
    
    B1 --> E3
    B1 --> E4
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:36-251](), [src/atomworks/io/utils/sequence.py:80-154]()

## Core TokenEncoding Class

The `TokenEncoding` class is the foundation of the encoding system, providing a standardized interface for converting between biological sequences and numerical representations.

### Key Components

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class TokenEncoding {
        +dict token_atoms
        +dict chemcomp_type_to_unknown
        +np.ndarray tokens
        +int n_tokens
        +int n_atoms_per_token
        +dict token_to_idx
        +dict atom_to_idx
        +resolve_unknown_token_name()
        +to_str()
    }
    
    class SequenceUtils {
        +get_1_from_3_letter_code()
        +get_3_from_1_letter_code()
        +aa_chem_comp_3to1()
        +na_chem_comp_3to1()
    }
    
    class CCDIntegration {
        +get_chem_comp_type()
        +atom_array_from_ccd_code()
        +chem_comp_to_one_letter()
    }
    
    TokenEncoding --> SequenceUtils : uses
    TokenEncoding --> CCDIntegration : uses
```

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `token_atoms` | `dict[str, np.ndarray]` | Maps residue names to ordered atom name arrays |
| `chemcomp_type_to_unknown` | `dict[str, str]` | Maps chemical component types to unknown tokens |
| `tokens` | `np.ndarray` | Array of all token names in the encoding |
| `n_tokens` | `int` | Total number of tokens in the encoding |
| `n_atoms_per_token` | `int` | Fixed number of atom positions per token |

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:36-109](), [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:158-221]()

### Unknown Token Resolution

The encoding system handles unknown residues and atoms through a hierarchical fallback mechanism:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Input: token_name, token_is_atom"] --> B{"Token in encoding?"}
    B -->|Yes| C["Return token_name"]
    B -->|No| D{"Is atom token?"}
    D -->|Yes| E{"UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_TOKEN in encoding?"}
    E -->|Yes| F["Return UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_TOKEN (0)"]
    E -->|No| G["Raise KeyError"]
    D -->|No| H{"chemcomp_type_to_unknown defined?"}
    H -->|Yes| I["Get chem_comp_type from CCD"]
    I --> J{"Chem type in mapping?"}
    J -->|Yes| K["Return unknown token for type"]
    J -->|No| L["Raise KeyError with guidance"]
    H -->|No| M["Raise KeyError"]
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:111-156](), [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:222-223]()

## Predefined Model Encodings

The system provides several predefined encodings optimized for different ML models:

### AlphaFold 2 Encodings

| Encoding | Atoms per Token | Token Count | Purpose |
|----------|-----------------|-------------|---------|
| `AF2_ATOM14_ENCODING` | 14 | 21 | Standard AF2 protein encoding |
| `AF2_ATOM37_ENCODING` | 37 | 21 | Extended AF2 encoding with all atom types |

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "AF2_ATOM14_ENCODING"
        A1["ALA: [N, CA, C, O, CB, '', '', ...]"]
        A2["ARG: [N, CA, C, O, CB, CG, CD, NE, CZ, NH1, NH2, '', '', '']"]
        A3["TRP: [N, CA, C, O, CB, CG, CD1, CD2, NE1, CE2, CE3, CZ2, CZ3, CH2]"]
        A4["UNK: ['', '', '', '', '', '', '', '', '', '', '', '', '', '']"]
    end
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:254-286](), [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:288-332]()

### RoseTTAFold 2 All-Atom Encodings

RF2AA provides multiple encoding granularities for different use cases:

| Encoding | Atoms per Token | Supports | Purpose |
|----------|-----------------|----------|---------|
| `RF2_ATOM14_ENCODING` | 14 | Proteins only | Protein-focused encoding |
| `RF2_ATOM23_ENCODING` | 23 | Proteins + DNA/RNA | Multi-molecule support |
| `RF2_ATOM36_ENCODING` | 36 | All molecular types + elements | Universal encoding |

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "RF2_ATOM36_ENCODING Coverage"
        B1["`Proteins (20 standard AA)
        ALA, ARG, ASN, ..., UNK`"]
        B2["`DNA (4 bases + unknown)
        DA, DC, DG, DT, DN`"]
        B3["`RNA (4 bases + unknown)
        A, C, G, U, N`"]
        B4["`Elements (atomic numbers)
        6 (Carbon), 7 (Nitrogen), 8 (Oxygen), ...`"]
        B5["`Special tokens
        <M> (mask), 0 (unknown element)`"]
    end
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:422-448](), [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:455-488](), [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:490-560]()

### Sequence Type Detection

The system automatically handles different molecular types through chemical component type detection:

| Chemical Component Type | Chain Type | 1-letter → 3-letter Example |
|------------------------|------------|------------------------------|
| `L-PEPTIDE LINKING` | `POLYPEPTIDE_L` | `A` → `ALA` |
| `DNA LINKING` | `DNA` | `A` → `DA` |
| `RNA LINKING` | `RNA` | `A` → `A` |

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/utils/sequence.py:106-112](), [src/atomworks/io/utils/ccd.py:560-596]()

## Integration with Chemical Component Dictionary

The encoding system leverages the Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD) for robust residue identification and unknown token handling:

```mermaid
graph TB
```

## MSA and Sequence Encoding

For Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) processing, the system provides specialized integer mappings:

| Sequence Type | Encoding Range | Unknown Token | Gap Token |
|---------------|----------------|---------------|-----------|
| Amino Acids | 0-26 | `X` (21) | `-` (20) |
| RNA Nucleotides | 27-41 | `N` (31) | `-` (20) |

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "MSA Integer Encoding"
        A1["`AMINO_ACID_ONE_LETTER_TO_INT
        A:0, R:1, ..., X:21`"]
        A2["`RNA_NUCLEOTIDE_ONE_LETTER_TO_INT
        A:27, C:28, G:29, U:30, N:31`"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Lookup Tables"
        B1["AMINO_ACID_ONE_LETTER_ASCII_TO_INT_LOOKUP_TABLE"]
        B2["RNA_NUCLEOTIDE_ONE_LETTER_ASCII_TO_INT_LOOKUP_TABLE"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Conversion Mappings"
        C1["MSA_INTEGER_TO_THREE_LETTER"]
        C2["THREE_LETTER_TO_MSA_INTEGER"]
    end
    
    A1 --> B1
    A2 --> B2
    B1 --> C1
    B2 --> C1
    C1 --> C2
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/msa/_msa_constants.py:43-154]()

## Usage in Transform Pipelines

Token encodings integrate with the broader ML transform system through encoding transforms that convert AtomArray structures to numerical tensors:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant AA as AtomArray
    participant ET as EncodeAtomArray Transform
    participant TE as TokenEncoding
    participant ML as ML Model
    
    AA->>ET: Structure with residue names
    ET->>TE: resolve_unknown_token_name()
    TE->>ET: Standardized token indices
    ET->>TE: atom_to_idx lookup
    TE->>ET: Atom position indices
    ET->>ML: Numerical tensors
```

The encoding system supports both residue-level and atom-level tokenization, enabling flexible model architectures from coarse-grained sequence models to fine-grained atomic structure models.

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:36-251](), [src/atomworks/io/utils/sequence.py:1-185]()

# Page: Model-Specific Pipelines

# Model-Specific Pipelines

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py](src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py)
- [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py](src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py)
- [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/encoding.py](src/atomworks/ml/transforms/encoding.py)
- [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/template.py](src/atomworks/ml/transforms/template.py)
- [tests/io/components/test_regression.py](tests/io/components/test_regression.py)
- [tests/io/tools/test_rdkit.py](tests/io/tools/test_rdkit.py)
- [tests/ml/conftest.py](tests/ml/conftest.py)
- [tests/ml/transforms/msa/test_featurize_msa.py](tests/ml/transforms/msa/test_featurize_msa.py)
- [tests/ml/utils/test_io.py](tests/ml/utils/test_io.py)

</details>



This page documents the model-specific transformation pipelines in AtomWorks that prepare molecular data for specific ML models. These pipelines build on the general transform system (see [Transform Pipeline](#3.1)) and token encoding schemes (see [Token Encodings](#3.2)) to create complete data processing workflows tailored for AlphaFold 3 (AF3) and RoseTTAFold 2 All-Atom (RF2AA) models.

Model-specific pipelines handle the complex orchestration of data preprocessing, feature engineering, and format conversion required by each model architecture. They encapsulate model-specific requirements such as cropping strategies, MSA processing, template handling, and output formatting.

## Pipeline Architecture Overview

The model-specific pipelines follow a common architectural pattern while implementing model-specific requirements:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Pipeline Components"
        A1["Data Preparation"] --> A2["Structural Processing"]
        A2 --> A3["Feature Engineering"] 
        A3 --> A4["Model-Specific Formatting"]
    end
    
    subgraph "AF3 Pipeline"
        B1["build_af3_transform_pipeline()"] --> B2["AF3 Cropping"]
        B2 --> B3["AF3 MSA Processing"]
        B3 --> B4["Diffusion Preparation"]
        B4 --> B5["Confidence Features"]
    end
    
    subgraph "RF2AA Pipeline"  
        C1["build_rf2aa_transform_pipeline()"] --> C2["RF2AA Cropping"]
        C2 --> C3["RF2AA MSA Processing"]
        C3 --> C4["Symmetry Resolution"]
        C4 --> C5["RF2AAInputs Format"]
    end
    
    A1 -.-> B1
    A1 -.-> C1
```

**Pipeline Builder Functions**
- AF3: `build_af3_transform_pipeline`
- RF2AA: `build_rf2aa_transform_pipeline`

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py:84-133](), [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py:154-205]()

## AF3 Pipeline Implementation

The AF3 pipeline implements the data processing workflow for AlphaFold 3, emphasizing diffusion-based structure generation and confidence estimation.

### Core Pipeline Function

The `build_af3_transform_pipeline` function constructs the complete AF3 processing pipeline:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "AF3 Pipeline Stages"
        A1["RemoveHydrogens"] --> A2["FilterToSpecifiedPNUnits"]
        A2 --> A3["HandleUndesiredResTokens"] 
        A3 --> A4["AtomizeByCCDName"]
        A4 --> A5["Cropping (Conditional)"]
        A5 --> A6["Template Loading"]
        A6 --> A7["MSA Processing"]
        A7 --> A8["Feature Aggregation"]
        A8 --> A9["Diffusion Preparation"]
        A9 --> A10["Confidence Features (Optional)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Key AF3 Components"
        B1["CropContiguousLikeAF3"]
        B2["CropSpatialLikeAF3"] 
        B3["FeaturizeTemplatesLikeAF3"]
        B4["FeaturizeMSALikeAF3"]
        B5["BatchStructuresForDiffusionNoising"]
        B6["SampleEDMNoise"]
        B7["PackageConfidenceFeats"]
    end
    
    A5 -.-> B1
    A5 -.-> B2
    A6 -.-> B3
    A7 -.-> B4
    A9 -.-> B5
    A9 -.-> B6
    A10 -.-> B7
```

**Key Parameters:**
- `is_inference`: Controls training vs inference behavior
- `crop_size`: Token limit for spatial/contiguous cropping
- `diffusion_batch_size`: Batch size for diffusion noising
- `run_confidence_head`: Enable confidence feature generation

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py:84-403]()

### AF3-Specific Features

#### Diffusion Preparation
The AF3 pipeline includes specialized transforms for diffusion-based structure generation:

| Transform | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `BatchStructuresForDiffusionNoising` | Prepares structures for noise sampling |
| `CenterRandomAugmentation` | Applies random centering augmentation |
| `SampleEDMNoise` | Samples noise using EDM (Elucidated Diffusion Models) |

#### Confidence Head Support
When `run_confidence_head=True`, the pipeline adds confidence-specific features:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["EncodeAtomArray"] --> B["AddAtomFrames"]
    B --> C["AddIsRealAtom"] 
    C --> D["AddPolymerFrameIndices"]
    D --> E["PackageConfidenceFeats"]
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py:355-375]()

#### Cropping Strategy
AF3 implements conditional cropping with configurable probabilities:

- **Training**: Random selection between contiguous and spatial cropping
- **Inference**: No cropping applied (`Identity` transform)

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py:213-244]()

## RF2AA Pipeline Implementation  

The RF2AA pipeline processes data for RoseTTAFold 2 All-Atom, emphasizing symmetry resolution and clustered MSA processing.

### Core Pipeline Function

The `build_rf2aa_transform_pipeline` function creates the RF2AA processing workflow:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "RF2AA Pipeline Stages"
        A1["Structure Preparation"] --> A2["Atomization"]
        A2 --> A3["OpenBabel Integration"]
        A3 --> A4["Cropping (Conditional)"]
        A4 --> A5["Encoding"]
        A5 --> A6["MSA Loading & Pairing"]
        A6 --> A7["Template Processing"]
        A7 --> A8["Feature Engineering"]
        A8 --> A9["Symmetry Resolution"]
        A9 --> A10["Feature Aggregation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "RF2AA Components"
        B1["AddOpenBabelMoleculesForAtomizedMolecules"]
        B2["FeaturizeMSALikeRF2AA"]
        B3["FeaturizeTemplatesLikeRF2AA"]
        B4["CreateSymmetryCopyAxisLikeRF2AA"]
        B5["AggregateFeaturesLikeRF2AA"]
        B6["RF2AAInputs"]
    end
    
    A3 -.-> B1
    A6 -.-> B2
    A7 -.-> B3
    A9 -.-> B4
    A10 -.-> B5
    A10 -.-> B6
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py:154-476]()

### RF2AA-Specific Features

#### Symmetry Resolution
RF2AA includes sophisticated symmetry handling for both polymers and small molecules:

| Parameter | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `max_automorphs` | Limit automorphs for small molecule symmetry |
| `max_isomorphs` | Limit polymer isomorphisms |
| `CreateSymmetryCopyAxisLikeRF2AA` | Generate symmetry copies |

#### OpenBabel Integration
RF2AA uniquely integrates OpenBabel for enhanced small molecule processing:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["AddOpenBabelMoleculesForAtomizedMolecules"] --> B["GetChiralCentersFromOpenBabel"]
    B --> C["Bond Feature Processing"]
```

#### MSA Clustering
RF2AA implements clustered MSA processing with masking:

- **Cluster Representatives**: Selected based on `n_msa_cluster_representatives`
- **Extra Rows**: Additional sequences for diversity
- **BERT-style Masking**: Applied to cluster representatives

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py:421-429]()

#### Output Format
RF2AA produces structured outputs via the `RF2AAInputs` named tuple:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `seq` | `np.ndarray` | Encoded sequence |
| `msa` | `np.ndarray` | MSA features |
| `xyz` | `np.ndarray` | Coordinate features |
| `mask` | `np.ndarray` | Validity masks |
| `bond_feats` | `np.ndarray` | Bond connectivity |
| `chirals` | `np.ndarray` | Chirality features |

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py:71-98]()

## Key Pipeline Differences

The AF3 and RF2AA pipelines differ in several fundamental ways:

### Processing Philosophy

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "AF3 Approach"
        A1["Diffusion-Based Generation"]
        A2["Dense MSA Processing"]
        A3["Confidence Estimation"]
        A4["Reference Molecule Features"]
    end
    
    subgraph "RF2AA Approach"
        B1["Energy-Based Optimization"]
        B2["Clustered MSA Processing"]
        B3["Symmetry Resolution"]
        B4["Explicit Bond Modeling"]
    end
```

### Technical Differences

| Aspect | AF3 | RF2AA |
|--------|-----|-------|
| **MSA Processing** | `FeaturizeMSALikeAF3` (dense) | `FeaturizeMSALikeRF2AA` (clustered) |
| **Cropping** | Contiguous/Spatial with probabilities | Similar but different parameters |
| **Small Molecules** | Reference molecule approach | OpenBabel integration |
| **Output Format** | Dictionary with feature keys | `RF2AAInputs` structured format |
| **Symmetry** | Limited symmetry handling | Extensive automorph/isomorph resolution |

### Usage Patterns

Both pipelines are typically instantiated through dataset wrappers in test configurations:

**AF3 Usage:**
```python
# From test configurations
af3_dataset = StructuralDatasetWrapper(
    dataset_parser=PNUnitsDFParser(),
    transform=build_af3_transform_pipeline(
        protein_msa_dirs=PROTEIN_MSA_DIRS,
        is_inference=False,
        diffusion_batch_size=32
    )
)
```

**RF2AA Usage:**
```python
# From test configurations  
rf2aa_dataset = StructuralDatasetWrapper(
    dataset_parser=PNUnitsDFParser(),
    transform=build_rf2aa_transform_pipeline(
        protein_msa_dirs=PROTEIN_MSA_DIRS,
        convert_feats_to_rf2aa_input_tuple=True
    )
)
```

Sources: [tests/ml/conftest.py:300-365](), [tests/ml/conftest.py:224-292]()

## Pipeline Configuration

Both pipelines support extensive configuration through their builder functions, enabling adaptation to different training and inference scenarios. The configuration parameters control data processing behavior, computational trade-offs, and model-specific feature generation requirements.

For dataset integration and broader ML workflow context, see [Dataset Management](#3.4).

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py](), [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py](), [tests/ml/conftest.py]()

# Page: Dataset Management

# Dataset Management

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/workflows/release_and_docs.yaml](.github/workflows/release_and_docs.yaml)

- [docs/_static/atomworks_logo_light.svg](docs/_static/atomworks_logo_light.svg)

This page documents the dataset management system in `atomworks.ml`, which provides infrastructure for loading, filtering, and wrapping biological datasets for machine learning workflows. The system handles both metadata-driven sampling from large databases like the PDB and direct data loading for training and inference.

For information about the transform pipelines that process dataset outputs, see [Transform Pipeline](#3.1). For model-specific pipeline configurations, see [Model-Specific Pipelines](#3.3).

## Core Architecture

The dataset management system consists of three main layers: dataset parsers that extract examples from data sources, dataset wrappers that apply transforms and handle batching, and configuration systems that coordinate the components.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Data Sources"
        A["pn_units_df.parquet"]
        B["interfaces_df.parquet"] 
        C["PDB mmCIF files"]
        D["MSA files"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Dataset Parsers"
        E["PNUnitsDFParser"]
        F["InterfacesDFParser"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Dataset Wrappers"
        G["PandasDataset"]
        H["StructuralDatasetWrapper"]
        I["ConcatDatasetWithID"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Transform Integration"
        J["Transform Pipeline"]
        K["AtomArray Output"]
    end
    
    A --> E
    B --> F
    E --> G
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    H --> J
    J --> K
    C --> H
    D --> H
```

**Dataset Management Architecture**

Sources: [README.md:182-262]()

## Dataset Parsers

Dataset parsers extract individual examples from structured data sources and convert them into loadable formats for ML workflows.

### PNUnitsDFParser

The `PNUnitsDFParser` processes metadata for individual polymer and non-polymer units (chains, ligands) from PDB structures. It reads from parquet files containing per-unit metadata and generates example IDs that can be loaded as individual structures.

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["pn_units_df.parquet"] --> B["PNUnitsDFParser"]
    B --> C["Example IDs"]
    C --> D["Individual PDB chains/ligands"]
    
    subgraph "Metadata Columns"
        E["deposition_date"]
        F["resolution"] 
        G["method"]
        H["cluster"]
        I["q_pn_unit_type"]
    end
    
    A -.-> E
    A -.-> F
    A -.-> G
    A -.-> H
    A -.-> I
```

**PNUnitsDFParser Data Flow**

The parser supports filtering based on metadata columns such as resolution, deposition date, experimental method, and chain type. Common filters include excluding NMR structures, setting resolution cutoffs, and selecting specific polymer types.

Sources: [README.md:186-221]()

### InterfacesDFParser

The `InterfacesDFParser` handles binary interface metadata, processing parquet files that contain information about protein-protein, protein-ligand, and other molecular interfaces within PDB structures.

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["interfaces_df.parquet"] --> B["InterfacesDFParser"]
    B --> C["Interface Example IDs"]
    C --> D["PDB interface regions"]
    
    subgraph "Interface Metadata"
        E["pn_unit_1_type"]
        F["pn_unit_2_type"]
        G["interface_area"]
        H["num_polymer_pn_units"]
    end
    
    A -.-> E
    A -.-> F
    A -.-> G
    A -.-> H
```

**InterfacesDFParser Data Flow**

Interface examples include spatial cropping around interaction regions and support filtering based on interface properties, partner types, and structural quality metrics.

Sources: [README.md:223-261]()

## Dataset Wrappers

Dataset wrappers coordinate between parsers, transforms, and the broader ML pipeline, handling data loading, filtering, and preprocessing.

### PandasDataset

The `PandasDataset` class provides the foundation for metadata-driven dataset loading. It loads parquet files, applies user-defined filters, and generates example IDs for downstream processing.

| Configuration | Purpose | Example |
|---------------|---------|---------|
| `data` | Path to parquet file | `/path/to/metadata/pn_units_df.parquet` |
| `filters` | List of pandas query strings | `["resolution < 5.0", "method in ['X-RAY_DIFFRACTION']"]` |
| `id_column` | Column containing example IDs | `"example_id"` |
| `columns_to_load` | Subset of columns to load | `null` (load all) |

```mermaid
graph TB
    A["Parquet File"] --> B["PandasDataset"]
    B --> C["Apply Filters"]
    C --> D["Extract Example IDs"]
    D --> E["StructuralDatasetWrapper"]
    
    subgraph "Filter Examples"
        F["deposition_date < '2022-01-01'"]
        G["resolution < 5.0"]
        H["method in ['X-RAY_DIFFRACTION']"]
        I["q_pn_unit_type in [5, 6]"]
    end
    
    C -.-> F
    C -.-> G
    C -.-> H
    C -.-> I
```

**PandasDataset Processing Flow**

Sources: [README.md:205-220](), [README.md:242-258]()

### StructuralDatasetWrapper

The `StructuralDatasetWrapper` coordinates between dataset parsers and transform pipelines, loading structural data based on example IDs and applying the configured transform pipeline.

```mermaid
graph TB
    A["Dataset Parser"] --> B["StructuralDatasetWrapper"]
    B --> C["Load PDB/mmCIF"]
    C --> D["Apply Transform Pipeline"]
    D --> E["Output AtomArray"]
    
    subgraph "Components"
        F["dataset_parser"]
        G["transform"] 
        H["dataset"]
        I["cif_parser_args"]
    end
    
    B -.-> F
    B -.-> G
    B -.-> H
    B -.-> I
    
    subgraph "Error Handling"
        J["save_failed_examples_to_dir"]
        K["Log parsing failures"]
    end
    
    D -.-> J
    D -.-> K
```

**StructuralDatasetWrapper Architecture**

The wrapper handles file loading from PDB mirrors, applies data cleaning and featurization transforms, and manages error handling for failed examples.

Sources: [README.md:185-188](), [README.md:224-227]()

### ConcatDatasetWithID

The `ConcatDatasetWithID` class combines multiple dataset sources (e.g., single chains and interfaces) into a unified training dataset while preserving example identification.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Dataset Sources"
        A["PN Units Dataset"]
        B["Interfaces Dataset"]
        C["Custom Dataset"]
    end
    
    D["ConcatDatasetWithID"] 
    A --> D
    B --> D
    C --> D
    
    subgraph "Unified Output"
        E["Combined Example Stream"]
        F["Preserved IDs"]
        G["Mixed Sampling"]
    end
    
    D --> E
    D --> F
    D --> G
```

**ConcatDatasetWithID Structure**

This enables training on diverse example types within a single pipeline, supporting mixed sampling strategies across different data modalities.

Sources: [README.md:183-184]()

## Configuration Patterns

Dataset management integrates with Hydra configuration to enable declarative pipeline definition through YAML files.

### Hydra Integration

```yaml
af3_pdb_dataset:
  _target_: atomworks.ml.datasets.datasets.ConcatDatasetWithID
  datasets:
    - _target_: atomworks.ml.datasets.datasets.StructuralDatasetWrapper
      dataset_parser:
        _target_: atomworks.ml.datasets.parsers.PNUnitsDFParser
      dataset:
        _target_: atomworks.ml.datasets.datasets.PandasDataset
        data: /path/to/metadata/pn_units_df.parquet
        filters:
          - "deposition_date < '2022-01-01'"
          - "resolution < 5.0"
```

### Transform Pipeline Integration

Dataset wrappers connect to transform pipelines through the `transform` parameter, enabling model-specific data processing:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["StructuralDatasetWrapper"] --> B["AF3 Transform Pipeline"]
    A --> C["RF2AA Transform Pipeline"] 
    A --> D["Custom Transform Pipeline"]
    
    subgraph "Transform Outputs"
        E["AF3 Features"]
        F["RF2AA Features"]
        G["Custom Features"]
    end
    
    B --> E
    C --> F
    D --> G
```

**Transform Pipeline Integration**

Sources: [README.md:189-200](), [README.md:228-241]()

## Usage Examples

### Basic Single Dataset

```yaml
single_chain_dataset:
  _target_: atomworks.ml.datasets.datasets.StructuralDatasetWrapper
  dataset_parser:
    _target_: atomworks.ml.datasets.parsers.PNUnitsDFParser
  dataset:
    _target_: atomworks.ml.datasets.datasets.PandasDataset
    data: /path/to/pn_units_df.parquet
    filters:
      - "q_pn_unit_type in [5, 6]"  # Polypeptides only
  transform:
    _target_: atomworks.ml.pipelines.af3.build_af3_transform_pipeline
```

### Multi-Source Training Dataset

The system supports combining multiple data sources with different sampling strategies:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Training Configuration"
        A["Single Chains"]
        B["Binary Interfaces"] 
        C["Custom Examples"]
    end
    
    D["ConcatDatasetWithID"]
    A --> D
    B --> D
    C --> D
    
    subgraph "Shared Components"
        E["Common Transform Pipeline"]
        F["Unified Batching"]
        G["Error Handling"]
    end
    
    D --> E
    D --> F
    D --> G
```

**Multi-Source Dataset Architecture**

This enables training on diverse molecular contexts while maintaining consistent preprocessing and batching across example types.

Sources: [README.md:165-275]()

## Error Handling and Debugging

The dataset system includes comprehensive error handling for production ML workflows:

| Feature | Purpose | Configuration |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| Failed example logging | Track parsing failures | `save_failed_examples_to_dir` |
| Parser arguments | Custom CIF parsing | `cif_parser_args` |
| Cache control | Manage temporary files | `cache_dir` |
| Column filtering | Reduce memory usage | `columns_to_load` |

Failed examples are logged with detailed error information to enable debugging and data quality analysis.

Sources: [README.md:221](), [README.md:260-261]()

# Command Line Interface

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

The AtomWorks CLI provides data management utilities for synchronizing biological databases and setting up development environments. The CLI enables users to maintain local mirrors of the RCSB PDB and PDBeChem CCD archives, as well as automate test environment preparation.

This page covers the overall CLI architecture and command structure. For detailed information about database synchronization, see [Data Synchronization](#4.1). For test environment setup procedures, see [Test Environment Setup](#4.2).

## CLI Architecture

The AtomWorks CLI is built using the `typer` framework and organized into three main command groups: `pdb`, `ccd`, and `setup`. Each group provides specialized functionality for different aspects of data management.

### Command Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    CLI["atomworks CLI<br/>(__main__.py)"]
    
    subgraph "Command Groups"
        PDB["pdb<br/>(pdb.py)"]
        CCD["ccd<br/>(ccd.py)"]  
        SETUP["setup<br/>(setup.py)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PDB Commands"
        PDB_SYNC["pdb sync<br/>sync_pdb()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "CCD Commands"  
        CCD_SYNC["ccd sync<br/>sync_ccd()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Setup Commands"
        SETUP_METADATA["setup metadata<br/>setup_metadata()"]
        SETUP_TESTS["setup tests<br/>setup_tests()"]
    end
    
    CLI --> PDB
    CLI --> CCD
    CLI --> SETUP
    
    PDB --> PDB_SYNC
    CCD --> CCD_SYNC
    SETUP --> SETUP_METADATA
    SETUP --> SETUP_TESTS
```

**CLI Command Hierarchy**

The main CLI application is defined in [src/atomworks/cli/__init__.py:7]() as a `typer.Typer` instance. Sub-applications are registered using `app.add_typer()` calls at [src/atomworks/cli/__init__.py:15-17]().

Sources: [src/atomworks/cli/__init__.py:1-18](), [src/atomworks/cli/__main__.py:1-14]()

### Application Entry Point

The CLI is accessible through multiple entry points:

| Entry Method | Command |
|--------------|---------|
| Module execution | `python -m atomworks.cli` |
| Direct execution | `atomworks <command>` |
| Package entry point | Configured in `pyproject.toml` |

The entry point is implemented in [src/atomworks/cli/__main__.py:8-9]() with a simple `main()` function that calls the root `app()`.

Sources: [src/atomworks/cli/__main__.py:8-14]()

## Data Synchronization Overview

### Remote Data Sources

The CLI connects to external biological databases to maintain local mirrors:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Remote Sources"
        PDB_REMOTE["rsync.wwpdb.org:33444<br/>RCSB PDB Archive"]
        CCD_REMOTE["ftp.ebi.ac.uk<br/>PDBeChem CCD"]
        METADATA_REMOTE["Pre-computed Metadata<br/>(PN units & interfaces)"]
        TEST_REMOTE["files.ipd.uw.edu<br/>Test Data Pack"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Synchronization Tools"
        RSYNC["rsync utility<br/>(-rltvz --stats)"]
        HTTP["urllib.request<br/>(with tqdm progress)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Local Storage"
        PDB_MIRROR["PDB Mirror<br/>(divided mmCIF layout)"]
        CCD_MIRROR["CCD Mirror<br/>(hierarchical CIF structure)"]
        METADATA_DIR["Metadata Directory<br/>(pn_units_df.parquet<br/>interfaces_df.parquet)"]
        TEST_DATA["Test Environment<br/>(tests/data/)"]
    end
    
    PDB_REMOTE --> RSYNC
    CCD_REMOTE --> RSYNC
    METADATA_REMOTE --> HTTP
    TEST_REMOTE --> HTTP
    
    RSYNC --> PDB_MIRROR
    RSYNC --> CCD_MIRROR
    HTTP --> METADATA_DIR
    HTTP --> TEST_DATA
```

**Data Source Configuration**

Remote endpoints are defined as constants in each module:
- PDB: `PDB_REMOTE` and `PDB_PORT` in [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:18-19]()
- CCD: `CCD_REMOTE` in [src/atomworks/cli/ccd.py:18]()
- Test pack: `TEST_PACK_URL` in [src/atomworks/cli/setup.py:18]()

Sources: [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:18-19](), [src/atomworks/cli/ccd.py:18](), [src/atomworks/cli/setup.py:18]()

### Synchronization Strategies

The CLI supports two synchronization modes for database mirrors:

| Mode | Description | Use Case |
|------|-------------|----------|
| Full sync | Complete mirror of entire database | Initial setup, comprehensive datasets |
| Selective sync | Specific entries only | Development, testing, targeted workflows |

Both PDB and CCD synchronization commands accept entry lists via command-line arguments (`--pdb-id`, `--ccd-code`) or input files (`--pdb-ids-file`, `--ccd-codes-file`).

## Environment Integration

### Environment Variables

The CLI integrates with environment-based configuration for database paths:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "CLI Commands"
        PDB_SYNC["pdb sync"]
        CCD_SYNC["ccd sync"]
        SETUP_TESTS["setup tests"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Environment Configuration"
        PDB_ENV["PDB_MIRROR_PATH"]
        CCD_ENV["CCD_MIRROR_PATH"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Local Filesystem"
        PDB_DIR["PDB Mirror Directory"]
        CCD_DIR["CCD Mirror Directory"]
        TEST_DIR["tests/data/"]
    end
    
    PDB_SYNC --> PDB_DIR
    CCD_SYNC --> CCD_DIR
    SETUP_TESTS --> TEST_DIR
    
    PDB_ENV -.-> PDB_DIR
    CCD_ENV -.-> CCD_DIR
    
    PDB_SYNC -.-> PDB_ENV
    CCD_SYNC -.-> CCD_ENV
    SETUP_TESTS --> PDB_ENV
```

**Environment Variable Usage**

After successful synchronization, the CLI provides instructions for setting environment variables. For example, the PDB sync command outputs setup instructions at [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:225-228]().

Sources: [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:225-228](), [src/atomworks/cli/ccd.py:258-262](), [src/atomworks/cli/setup.py:87]()

## Error Handling and Validation

### Connection Testing

Both PDB and CCD synchronization commands perform connectivity tests before attempting data transfer:

```mermaid
graph TD
    SYNC_START["Sync Command Initiated"]
    CONN_TEST["Connection Test<br/>(_run_rsync_list)"]
    CONN_SUCCESS{"Connection<br/>Successful?"}
    SYNC_EXEC["Execute Sync<br/>(rsync commands)"]
    ERROR_EXIT["Display Error & Exit"]
    SUCCESS["Sync Complete<br/>(Write README)"]
    
    SYNC_START --> CONN_TEST
    CONN_TEST --> CONN_SUCCESS
    CONN_SUCCESS -->|Yes| SYNC_EXEC
    CONN_SUCCESS -->|No| ERROR_EXIT
    SYNC_EXEC --> SUCCESS
```

**Connection Test Implementation**

The `_run_rsync_list()` function is implemented in both [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:40-52]() and [src/atomworks/cli/ccd.py:53-73]() to validate remote connectivity before attempting synchronization.

Sources: [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:40-52](), [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:192-199](), [src/atomworks/cli/ccd.py:53-73](), [src/atomworks/cli/ccd.py:229-236]()

### Input Validation

Entry ID validation ensures data integrity:

| Database | Validation Function | Pattern |
|----------|-------------------|---------|
| PDB | `_normalize_pdb_id()` | 4-character alphanumeric |
| CCD | `_normalize_ccd_code()` | 1-3 character uppercase |

Invalid entries are silently skipped during collection in `_collect_pdb_ids()` and `_collect_ccd_codes()` functions.

Sources: [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:22-27](), [src/atomworks/cli/ccd.py:21-34](), [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:117-139](), [src/atomworks/cli/ccd.py:149-180]()

## Integration with AtomWorks Ecosystem

The CLI serves as the entry point for data acquisition in the broader AtomWorks processing pipeline:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "CLI Layer"
        CLI_SYNC["CLI Sync Commands"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Storage"
        MIRRORS["Local Database Mirrors"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing Layer"
        PARSER["atomworks.io.parser"]
        ML_PIPELINE["atomworks.ml pipeline"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Applications"
        TRAINING["ML Training"]
        ANALYSIS["Structure Analysis"]
    end
    
    CLI_SYNC --> MIRRORS
    MIRRORS --> PARSER
    PARSER --> ML_PIPELINE
    ML_PIPELINE --> TRAINING
    PARSER --> ANALYSIS
```

**Data Flow Integration**

The CLI-maintained mirrors provide the raw data consumed by the `atomworks.io.parser` system documented in [Core Parser System](#2.1). Environment variables set by CLI commands configure parser data source locations.

Sources: [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:225-228](), [src/atomworks/cli/ccd.py:258-262](), [src/atomworks/cli/setup.py:134]()

# Data Synchronization

<details>

This document covers the AtomWorks CLI data synchronization system, which provides commands for maintaining local mirrors of biological data archives and downloading pre-computed metadata. The system enables users to synchronize PDB mmCIF files, obtain metadata for machine learning workflows, and set up test environments.

For information about test environment setup using synchronized data, see [Test Environment Setup](#4.2). For details about using synchronized data within the parsing system, see [Core Parser System](#2.1).

## Overview

The AtomWorks CLI provides three primary data synchronization commands:

- `atomworks pdb sync` - mirrors RCSB PDB mmCIF archive
- `atomworks setup metadata` - downloads pre-computed PDB metadata for ML workflows  
- `atomworks setup tests` - downloads test data and environments

The PDB synchronization uses rsync for bandwidth efficiency and resumable transfers. The metadata setup downloads pre-processed parquet files containing structural annotations and interface information.

### CLI Command Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "CLI Application"
        MAIN["atomworks CLI"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PDB Commands"
        PDB_SYNC["atomworks pdb sync"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Setup Commands"
        SETUP_METADATA["atomworks setup metadata"]
        SETUP_TESTS["atomworks setup tests"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Outputs"
        PDB_MIRROR["PDB Mirror Directory"]
        METADATA_FILES["Metadata Parquet Files"]
        TEST_DATA["Test Data Pack"]
    end
    
    MAIN --> PDB_SYNC
    MAIN --> SETUP_METADATA
    MAIN --> SETUP_TESTS
    
    PDB_SYNC --> PDB_MIRROR
    SETUP_METADATA --> METADATA_FILES
    SETUP_TESTS --> TEST_DATA
```

Sources: [README.md:128-163]()

## PDB Archive Synchronization

The PDB synchronization system maintains a local mirror of the RCSB PDB mmCIF archive using the divided directory structure. The system downloads compressed mmCIF files and organizes them in the standard PDB directory hierarchy.

### PDB Sync Process

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input Options"
        FULL_MIRROR["Full Mirror<br/>~100 GB"]
        SPECIFIC_IDS["Specific PDB IDs<br/>--pdb-id option"]
        IDS_FILE["PDB IDs from file<br/>--pdb-ids-file"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Sync Operation"
        RSYNC["rsync download"]
        REMOTE_PDB["RCSB PDB FTP"]
        LOCAL_MIRROR["Local PDB Mirror"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Structure"
        DIVIDED_DIRS["Divided Directories<br/>(e.g., a0/, xy/, ab/)"]
        MMCIF_FILES["mmCIF.gz files"]
        ENV_SETUP["PDB_MIRROR_PATH"]
    end
    
    FULL_MIRROR --> RSYNC
    SPECIFIC_IDS --> RSYNC
    IDS_FILE --> RSYNC
    
    REMOTE_PDB --> RSYNC
    RSYNC --> LOCAL_MIRROR
    
    LOCAL_MIRROR --> DIVIDED_DIRS
    DIVIDED_DIRS --> MMCIF_FILES
    LOCAL_MIRROR --> ENV_SETUP
```

Sources: [README.md:128-148]()

### PDB Directory Structure

The PDB sync maintains the official divided directory structure where files are organized by the middle two characters of the PDB ID:

| PDB ID | Subdirectory | File Path |
|--------|--------------|-----------|
| `1a0i` | `a0/` | `a0/1a0i.cif.gz` |
| `2xyz` | `xy/` | `xy/2xyz.cif.gz` |
| `7abc` | `ab/` | `ab/7abc.cif.gz` |

This organization matches the standard PDB FTP archive structure and enables efficient access to individual entries.

Sources: [README.md:128-148]()

## PDB Metadata Setup

The metadata setup system downloads pre-computed PDB metadata files required for machine learning workflows. These files contain processed information about protein structures, interfaces, and sampling probabilities.

### Metadata Setup Process

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Command"
        SETUP_CMD["atomworks setup metadata"]
        DEST_PATH["destination_path"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Download Process"
        REMOTE_TAR["Pre-computed metadata<br/>(tar.gz archive)"]
        DOWNLOAD["Download archive"]
        EXTRACT["Extract files"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Files"
        PN_UNITS["pn_units_df.parquet"]
        INTERFACES["interfaces_df.parquet"]
        METADATA_DIR["Metadata directory"]
    end
    
    SETUP_CMD --> DEST_PATH
    DEST_PATH --> DOWNLOAD
    REMOTE_TAR --> DOWNLOAD
    DOWNLOAD --> EXTRACT
    EXTRACT --> METADATA_DIR
    METADATA_DIR --> PN_UNITS
    METADATA_DIR --> INTERFACES
```

Sources: [README.md:150-163]()

### Metadata File Contents

The metadata setup produces two primary parquet files:

| File | Content | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `pn_units_df.parquet` | PN Unit metadata | Information about each polymer/non-polymer unit in the PDB |
| `interfaces_df.parquet` | Interface metadata | Binary interface information between PN units |

**PN Units**: The term "PN unit" is shorthand for "polymer XOR non-polymer unit" and behaves like PDB chains but treats covalently bonded ligands as single units.

**Interfaces**: Contains metadata for binary interfaces as (pn_unit_1, pn_unit_2) pairs with filtering and sampling information.

Sources: [README.md:158-161]()

## Usage Patterns

### Full Archive Synchronization

```bash
# Mirror complete PDB archive (~100 GB)
atomworks pdb sync /data/pdb-mirror

# Mirror complete CCD archive
atomworks ccd sync /data/ccd-mirror
```

### Selective Synchronization

```bash
# Sync specific PDB entries
atomworks pdb sync /data/pdb-mirror --pdb-id 1abc --pdb-id 2xyz

# Sync PDB entries from file
atomworks pdb sync /data/pdb-mirror --pdb-ids-file my_structures.txt

# Sync specific CCD entries
atomworks ccd sync /data/ccd-mirror --ccd-code ALA --ccd-code GLY
```

### Environment Configuration

After synchronization, the commands provide environment variable setup instructions:

```bash
export PDB_MIRROR_PATH=/data/pdb-mirror
export CCD_MIRROR_PATH=/data/ccd-mirror
```

These environment variables are used by the AtomWorks parsing system to locate local copies of structural data.

Sources: [src/atomworks/cli/pdb.py:225-228](), [src/atomworks/cli/ccd.py:259-262]()

# Test Environment Setup

This document covers setting up the test environment for AtomWorks development and evaluation. The test environment provides a minimal dataset with representative samples from the PDB, MSA data, templates, and metadata that enables testing and validation of ML pipelines without requiring full dataset downloads.

For information about setting up production PDB mirrors and metadata, see [Data Synchronization](#4.1). For overall project configuration and development setup, see [Project Configuration and Development](#5).

## Purpose and Scope

The test environment setup provides a streamlined way to:

- Download and configure test data (~500 MB) for development and validation
- Create a miniature version of the full PDB processing pipeline
- Test ML workflows including AF3 and RF2AA pipelines without full dataset requirements
- Validate data processing transforms and dataset loading functionality

## Test Data CLI Command

The primary interface for test environment setup is the `atomworks setup tests` command, which downloads and extracts a curated test dataset.

```bash
atomworks setup tests  # Downloads test pack to `tests/data` and unpacks it there (~500 MB)
```

This command creates a complete test environment with representative biological data samples that mirror the structure of production datasets.

Sources: [README.md:277-283]()

## Test Data Structure

The test setup creates a hierarchical directory structure that mirrors production data organization:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Test Data Directory Structure"
        TestsData["tests/data/"]
        
        subgraph "Structure Data"
            PDB["tests/data/pdb/"]
            CCD["tests/data/ccd/"]
        end
        
        subgraph "ML Support Data"
            Shared["tests/data/shared/"]
            Templates["Template data"]
            MSAs["MSA data"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Metadata"
            AF2Dist["data/ml/af2_distillation/"]
            PNUnits["data/ml/pdb_pn_units/"]
            Interfaces["data/ml/pdb_interfaces/"]
        end
    end
    
    TestsData --> PDB
    TestsData --> CCD
    TestsData --> Shared
    Shared --> Templates
    Shared --> MSAs
    TestsData --> AF2Dist
    TestsData --> PNUnits
    TestsData --> Interfaces
```

**Test Data Components:**

| Component | Location | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Mini PDB | `tests/data/pdb/` | Representative protein structure files |
| Custom CCD | `tests/data/ccd/` | Chemical Component Dictionary for ligands |
| MSA Data | `tests/data/shared/` | Multiple Sequence Alignments |
| Templates | `tests/data/shared/` | Template structures for modeling |
| AF2 Distillation | `data/ml/af2_distillation/` | AlphaFold2 distillation data |
| PN Units Metadata | `data/ml/pdb_pn_units/` | Polymer/non-polymer unit metadata |
| Interface Metadata | `data/ml/pdb_interfaces/` | Protein-protein interface data |

Sources: [README.md:280-283]()

The test environment integrates with the core AtomWorks systems to provide a complete testing framework:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
```

**Key Integration Points:**

- **Data Loading Validation**: Tests PandasDataset and StructuralDatasetWrapper functionality
- **Environment Variables**: Test setup respects `PDB_MIRROR_PATH` and other configuration

Sources: [README.md:283]()

## Running Test Pipelines

Once the test environment is set up, you can run comprehensive pipeline tests:

```bash
# Set up environment (if not already configured)
export PDB_MIRROR_PATH=/path/to/test/pdb

# Run ML pipeline tests
pytest tests/ml/test_data_loading_pipelines.py
```

The test framework validates:

- Data parsing and loading from test PDB files
- Transform pipeline execution with representative data
- Dataset filtering and sampling functionality
- MSA and template integration
- Metadata handling and validation

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Test Execution Flow"
        TestCommand["pytest tests/ml/test_data_loading_pipelines.py"]
        
        subgraph "Data Loading Tests"
            ParseTest["Test file parsing"]
            FilterTest["Test dataset filtering"]
            TransformTest["Test transform pipelines"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Pipeline Validation"
            AF3Test["AF3 pipeline validation"]
            RF2AATest["RF2AA pipeline validation"]
            FeatureTest["Feature engineering validation"]
        end
        
        subgraph "Integration Testing"
            MSATest["MSA integration test"]
            TemplateTest["Template integration test"]
            MetadataTest["Metadata validation test"]
        end
    end
    
    TestCommand --> ParseTest
    TestCommand --> FilterTest
    TestCommand --> TransformTest
    
    ParseTest --> AF3Test
    FilterTest --> RF2AATest
    TransformTest --> FeatureTest
    
    AF3Test --> MSATest
    RF2AATest --> TemplateTest
    FeatureTest --> MetadataTest
```

Sources: [README.md:285-290]()

## Test vs Production Environment Mapping

The test environment provides a scaled-down version of the production data processing pipeline:

| Production Component | Test Equivalent | Scale Factor |
|---------------------|----------------|--------------|
| Full PDB mirror (~100 GB) | `tests/data/pdb/` | ~500 MB total |
| Complete metadata | Sample metadata files | Representative subset |
| Full MSA databases | `tests/data/shared/` MSAs | Selected examples |
| Template databases | `tests/data/shared/` templates | Curated samples |
| Production configs | Test configurations | Simplified parameters |

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Production Pipeline"
        ProdPDB["Full PDB Mirror"]
        ProdMetadata["Complete Metadata"]
        ProdMSA["Full MSA Databases"]
        ProdTemplates["Template Databases"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Test Environment"
        TestPDB["Mini PDB"]
        TestMetadata["Sample Metadata"]
        TestMSA["Sample MSAs"]
        TestTemplates["Sample Templates"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Validation"
        SameAPI["Same API"]
        SameTransforms["Same Transforms"]
        SameWorkflows["Same Workflows"]
    end
    
    ProdPDB -.->|"Representative samples"| TestPDB
    ProdMetadata -.->|"Subset"| TestMetadata
    ProdMSA -.->|"Examples"| TestMSA
    ProdTemplates -.->|"Curated"| TestTemplates
    
    TestPDB --> SameAPI
    TestMetadata --> SameTransforms
    TestMSA --> SameWorkflows
    TestTemplates --> SameWorkflows
```

The test environment ensures that development and validation can proceed with the same APIs and workflows as production, while requiring significantly less storage and download time.

Sources: [README.md:277-283](), [README.md:128-164]()

This page covers the project configuration, development workflow, and infrastructure setup for AtomWorks. It includes package management, build system configuration, code quality tools, testing infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, documentation generation, and release management.

For information about the core data processing functionality, see [Data Processing Pipeline](#2.2). For details about the ML pipeline transforms and datasets, see [Transform Pipeline](#3.1).

## Project Structure and Package Configuration

AtomWorks uses a modern Python packaging setup with `pyproject.toml` as the central configuration file. The project follows a standard source layout with packages in the `src/` directory.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Package Structure"
        A["pyproject.toml"] --> B["src/atomworks/"]
        A --> C["src/atomworks_cli/"]
        B --> D["io/"]
        B --> E["ml/"] 
        B --> F["enums.py"]
        B --> G["constants.py"]
        C --> H["__main__.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Build System"
        I["hatchling"] --> J["hatch-vcs"]
        A --> I
        K["setup.py"] -.-> L["Legacy (not used)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Distribution"
        M["PyPI"] --> N["atomworks package"]
        O["GitHub Releases"] --> N
        P["semantic-release"] --> M
        P --> O
    end
```

**Package Configuration Details**

The main package configuration is defined in [pyproject.toml:1-91]():
- **Package metadata**: Name, version, description, authors, license
- **Python version requirement**: `>=3.12`
- **Entry points**: CLI command `atomworks` pointing to `atomworks_cli.__main__:main`
- **Build backend**: Uses `hatchling` with `hatch-vcs` for version management

Sources: `pyproject.toml`

## Dependencies and Optional Features

AtomWorks uses a tiered dependency system with core dependencies and optional feature groups to support different use cases.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Core Dependencies"
        A["numpy"] 
        B["scipy"]
        C["pandas"] 
        D["biotite"]
        E["rdkit"]
        F["typer"]
        G["cython"]
    end

    end

        M["pytest-cov"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Optional: docs"
        N["sphinx"]
        O["sphinx-gallery"]
        P["pydata-sphinx-theme"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Optional: openbabel"
        Q["openbabel-wheel"]
    end
```

**Installation Commands**

[pyproject.toml:57-68]() defines the installation patterns:
- Base: `pip install atomworks` (atomworks.io only)
- ML features: `pip install "atomworks[ml]"` (includes torch for atomworks.ml)
- Development: `pip install "atomworks[dev]"` (testing and linting tools)
- All features: `pip install "atomworks[ml,dev]"`

**Dependency Groups for uv**

[pyproject.toml:77-82]() also defines native uv compatibility via dependency groups, allowing usage with the modern `uv` package manager.

Sources: `pyproject.toml`

## Code Quality and Testing

AtomWorks uses Ruff for code formatting and linting, with pytest for testing. The configuration emphasizes code quality while remaining practical for scientific computing.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Code Quality Tools"
        A["ruff"] --> B["Format"]
        A --> C["Lint"]
        B --> D["line-length: 120"]
        B --> E["quote-style: double"]
        C --> F["Select Rules"]
        C --> G["Ignore Rules"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Ruff Rules"
        F --> H["E: pycodestyle errors"]
        F --> I["F: pyflakes"] 
        F --> J["W: pycodestyle warnings"]
        F --> K["I: isort"]
        F --> L["ANN: type annotations"]
        F --> M["NPY: numpy fixes"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Testing Framework"
        N["pytest"] --> O["Test Discovery"]
        N --> P["Parallel Execution"]
        N --> Q["Coverage Reports"]
        O --> R["tests/"]
        P --> S["pytest-xdist"]
        Q --> T["pytest-cov"]
    end
```

**Ruff Configuration**

[pyproject.toml:108-219]() contains comprehensive Ruff settings:
- **Line length**: 120 characters
- **Target version**: Python 3.12
- **Excluded directories**: Build artifacts, virtual environments, data directories
- **Format settings**: Double quotes, space indents, automatic line endings
- **Lint rules**: Comprehensive set including pycodestyle, pyflakes, isort, type annotations

**Test Configuration**

[pyproject.toml:222-254]() defines pytest configuration:
- **Test paths**: `tests` directory only
- **Import mode**: `importlib` for modern Python
- **Python path**: Includes `src/atomworks` and `tests`
- **Custom markers**: `requires_internet`, `requires_pymol_remote`, `requires_digs`, `slow`

**Coverage Settings**

Parallel test execution with coverage tracking, excluding version files and init files.

Sources: `pyproject.toml`

## CI/CD Pipeline

The project uses GitHub Actions for continuous integration and deployment with separate workflows for testing and releases.


**Testing Pipeline**

[.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yaml:1-132]() defines the testing workflow:
- **Triggers**: Push to main/production, PRs to main/dev/staging/production
- **Lint job**: Extracts Ruff version from pyproject.toml, runs format and lint checks
- **DIGS testing**: Runs on internal infrastructure with SLURM
- **GitHub testing**: Ubuntu runner with parallel test execution using pytest-xdist

**Release Pipeline**

[.github/workflows/release_and_docs.yaml:1-159]() handles releases and documentation:
- **Trigger**: Push to production branch
- **Package building**: Uses standard Python build tools
- **Semantic release**: Automated versioning and publishing to PyPI
- **Documentation**: Builds Sphinx docs and deploys versioned documentation

Sources: `.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yaml`, `.github/workflows/release_and_docs.yaml`

## Release Management

AtomWorks uses semantic-release for automated version management and publishing, following conventional commit standards.

```mermaid

    subgraph "Semantic Release Configuration"

        F --> K["@semantic-release/git"]
    end

        L["Commit to production"] --> M["Analyze Commits"]
        M --> N["Determine Version"]
        N --> O["Generate Changelog"]
        O --> P["Build Package"]
        P --> Q["Publish to PyPI"]
        Q --> R["Create GitHub Release"]

        S --> T["Deploy Documentation"]
    end
```

**Release Configuration**

[.releaserc.js:1-25]() defines the semantic release setup:
- **Branches**: Releases from `production` and `main` branches
- **Plugins**: Full pipeline from commit analysis to publication
- **PyPI integration**: Automated package publishing with token authentication
- **Git updates**: Automatic version bumping in pyproject.toml

**Version Management**

The system automatically:
- Analyzes conventional commits to determine version bump type
- Generates release notes from commit messages
- Updates package version in pyproject.toml
- Creates GitHub releases with generated changelogs
- Publishes to PyPI with built distributions

Sources: `.releaserc.js`, `.github/workflows/release_and_docs.yaml`

## Core Dependencies

AtomWorks is built on several foundational scientific computing and bioinformatics libraries. The core dependencies provide essential functionality for molecular data processing and analysis.

### Primary Dependencies

The project's core dependencies are defined in the `dependencies` section of [pyproject.toml:24-44]():

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Core Scientific Stack"
        numpy["numpy>=1.25.0,<3<br/>Linear algebra & arrays"]
        scipy["scipy>=1.13.1,<2<br/>Scientific computing"]
        pandas["pandas>=2.2,<2.4<br/>Data manipulation"]
        pyarrow["pyarrow==17.0.0<br/>Columnar data format"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Bioinformatics Libraries"
        biotite["biotite>=1.3.0,<2<br/>Protein structure analysis"]
        hydride["hydride>=1.2.3,<2<br/>Hydrogen addition"]
        rdkit["rdkit>=2024.3.5,<2025.9<br/>Cheminformatics"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization & Tools"
        py3dmol["py3Dmol>=2.2.1,<3<br/>3D molecular visualization"]
        pymol["pymol-remote>=0.0.5<br/>Remote PyMOL access"]
    end
    
    subgraph "System & Performance"
        cython["cython>=3.0.0,<4<br/>C extensions compiler"]
        cytoolz["cytoolz>=0.12.3,<1<br/>Functional programming"]
        tqdm["tqdm>=4.65.0,<5<br/>Progress bars"]
        typer["typer>=0.12.5,<1<br/>CLI framework"]
    end
    
    numpy --> biotite
    numpy --> rdkit
    scipy --> rdkit
    pandas --> pyarrow
    cython --> cytoolz
```

Sources: [pyproject.toml:24-44]()

### Key Dependency Relationships

The `biotite` library serves as the foundation for molecular structure handling throughout AtomWorks. It provides the `AtomArray` data structure that is central to the data processing pipeline, as seen in functions like `parse()` in the core parser system.

The `rdkit` library enables small molecule processing and cheminformatics functionality, particularly for handling SMILES strings and molecular descriptors. Integration points are visible in [src/atomworks/io/utils/sequence.py]() and related conversion utilities.

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/utils/ccd.py:8-13](), [src/atomworks/io/utils/sequence.py:11-32]()
