
This installs AtomWorks in editable mode with all optional dependencies, ensuring comprehensive testing of the full feature set.

Sources: [.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yaml:96-103]()

### Test Execution

The pipeline runs different test configurations:
- **GitHub Runners**: Standard tests excluding slow benchmarks
- **DIGS Infrastructure**: Full test suite including infrastructure-specific tests

This document covers the code quality standards, testing practices, and automated validation workflows used in AtomWorks. It explains the linting, formatting, testing frameworks, and continuous integration processes that ensure code reliability and maintainability.

For information about the CI/CD pipeline deployment and release processes, see [CI/CD Pipeline](#5.3). For details about project dependencies and build configuration, see [Dependencies and Build System](#5.1).

## Code Quality Standards

AtomWorks maintains code quality through automated linting, formatting, and comprehensive testing. The project uses modern Python tooling configured through `pyproject.toml` to enforce consistent code style and catch potential issues.

### Ruff Configuration

The project uses `ruff` as the primary tool for both code linting and formatting, providing a fast, unified approach to code quality enforcement.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "ruff_config"["Ruff Configuration"]
        A["pyproject.toml<br/>[tool.ruff]"] --> B["line-length: 120<br/>target-version: py312"]
        A --> C["[tool.ruff.lint]<br/>select rules"]
        A --> D["[tool.ruff.format]<br/>formatting options"]
        
        C --> E["pycodestyle (E, W)<br/>pyflakes (F)<br/>isort (I)"]
        C --> F["pep8-naming (N)<br/>pyupgrade (UP)<br/>flake8-bugbear (B)"]
        C --> G["flake8-comprehensions (C4)<br/>flake8-simplify (SIM)<br/>type annotations (ANN)"]
        
        D --> H["quote-style: double<br/>indent-style: space<br/>docstring-code-format: true"]
    end
    
    subgraph "excluded_dirs"["Excluded Directories"]
        I[".git, .pytest_cache<br/>.ruff_cache, .venv<br/>build, dist, data"]
    end
    
    A --> I
```

**Ruff Linting Rules**

The linting configuration enables a comprehensive set of rules for code quality:

| Rule Category | Code | Description |
|---------------|------|-------------|
| pycodestyle | E, W | Style guide enforcement |
| pyflakes | F | Logical errors and unused imports |
| isort | I | Import sorting and organization |
| pep8-naming | N | Naming convention enforcement |
| pyupgrade | UP | Modern Python syntax usage |
| flake8-bugbear | B | Bug-prone pattern detection |
| flake8-comprehensions | C4 | List/dict comprehension improvements |
| flake8-simplify | SIM | Code simplification suggestions |
| type annotations | ANN | Type hint enforcement |

**Sources:** [pyproject.toml:108-220]()

### Per-File Linting Exceptions

The configuration includes targeted exceptions for specific file types:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "per_file_ignores"["Per-File Ignore Rules"]
        A["__init__.py"] --> B["F401: unused imports"]
        C["tests/*"] --> D["D: docstring rules<br/>E: style errors<br/>ANN: type annotations"]
        E["docs/**/*.py"] --> F["E402: import positioning"]
        G["docs/**/*.ipynb"] --> H["E402: import positioning"]
    end
```

**Sources:** [pyproject.toml:204-208]()

AtomWorks uses `pytest` as the primary testing framework with several plugins to enhance testing capabilities and performance.

### Test Markers and Categories

The project defines custom pytest markers to categorize and selectively run tests:

| Marker | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `requires_internet` | Tests needing internet connectivity |
| `requires_pymol_remote` | Tests requiring PyMOL remote connection |
| `requires_x3dna` | Tests requiring X3DNA software |
| `requires_digs` | Tests for IPD DIGS infrastructure |
| `slow` | Long-running tests |

**Sources:** [pyproject.toml:227-232]()

## Continuous Integration Pipeline

### Lint and Test Workflow

The CI pipeline implements a two-stage approach with linting as a prerequisite for testing:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "ci_workflow"["CI/CD Lint and Test Workflow"]
        A["GitHub Push/PR"] --> B["lint job<br/>ruff check & format"]
        
        B --> C["test_github job<br/>Ubuntu latest"]
        B --> D["test_digs job<br/>jojo runner"]
        
        C --> E["Setup Python 3.12<br/>Install dependencies with uv"]
        C --> F["atomworks setup tests<br/>Download test data"]
        C --> G["pytest execution<br/>Parallel with xdist"]
        
        D --> H["SLURM execution<br/>srun with 8 CPUs"]
        
        G --> I["Coverage report<br/>Upload artifact"]
        H --> I
    end
```

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yaml:1-132]()

### Test Execution Strategy

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "test_execution"["Test Execution Patterns"]
        A["Single CPU"] --> B["Sequential execution<br/>io and ml tests separately"]
        C["Multi CPU"] --> D["Parallel execution<br/>pytest -n auto --maxprocesses"]
        
        E["Test Filtering"] --> F["-m 'not benchmark'<br/>Skip performance tests"]
        E --> G["-m 'not slow'<br/>Skip long-running tests"]
    end
```

The CI system adapts test execution based on available resources, running tests sequentially on single-CPU systems and in parallel on multi-CPU systems.

**Sources:** [.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yaml:110-125]()

### Environment Setup

This document covers the automated Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline that ensures code quality, runs comprehensive tests, and manages releases for the AtomWorks project. The pipeline includes automated linting, testing on multiple environments, semantic versioning, PyPI publishing, and versioned documentation deployment.

For information about project dependencies and build configuration, see [Dependencies and Build System](#5.1). For details about code quality tools and testing setup, see [Code Quality and Testing](#5.2).

## CI/CD Architecture Overview

The AtomWorks CI/CD pipeline is implemented through GitHub Actions workflows that automate releases and documentation deployment:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Trigger Events"
        A["Push to production branch"]
    end

        C["setup_node_js"]
        D["setup_python"]
        E["build_python_package"]
        F["install_node_dependencies"]
        G["run_semantic_release"]
        H["build_documentation"]
        I["checkout_gh_pages"]
        J["deploy_versioned_docs"]
        K["deploy_to_github_pages"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External Services"
        L["PyPI Registry"]
        M["GitHub Pages"]
        N["npm Registry"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Release Outputs"
        O["Git Tags"]
        P["GitHub Releases"]
        Q["PyPI Package"]
        R["Versioned Documentation"]
    end
    
    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I --> J
    J --> K

    K --> R
    F --> N
```

## Release and Documentation Deployment

The `release_and_docs` workflow handles automated releases when code is pushed to the `production` branch:

### Semantic Release Implementation

The complete release automation sequence follows this execution pattern:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Release_Execution_Flow"
        A["npx_semantic_release"]
        B["git_describe_tags"]
        C["echo_version_GITHUB_OUTPUT"]
        D["conditional_docs_deployment"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Version_Detection_Logic"
        E["VERSION=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 --match v* 2>/dev/null || echo no-version)"]
        F["echo version=$VERSION >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT"]
    end
    
    A --> B
    B --> C
    B --> E
    E --> F
    C --> D
```

The plugin configuration in `.releaserc.js` defines branch targeting and asset management:

```javascript
// Key configuration from .releaserc.js
branches: ['production', 'main']
pypiPublish: true
repoUrl: 'https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/'
distDir: 'dist/'
assets: ['pyproject.toml']
```

```bash
# Version directory pattern matching from workflow
if [[ "$d" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$d" == "latest" ]]; then
```

## Environment Variables and Secrets

The CI/CD pipeline uses GitHub Secrets for secure operations:

| Secret/Variable | Purpose | Workflow Usage |
|----------------|---------|----------------|
| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | GitHub API access | Release creation, Pages deployment |
| `PYPI_TOKEN` | PyPI publishing | `process.env.PYPI_TOKEN_PROD` in semantic-release |
| `PYPI_REPO_URL` | PyPI endpoint | `https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/` |

### Secret Configuration in Workflow

```yaml
# Environment variables in release_and_docs.yaml
env:
  GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  PYPI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN_PROD }}
  PYPI_REPO_URL: https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/
```

The semantic release configuration accesses these through Node.js environment variables:

```javascript
// .releaserc.js secret access
pypiToken: process.env.PYPI_TOKEN_PROD
```

**Sources**: [.github/workflows/release_and_docs.yaml:53-57](), [.releaserc.js:13]()

## Workflow Triggers and Concurrency

### Trigger Configuration

The workflows are triggered by specific events to optimize resource usage:

```yaml
# lint_and_test triggers
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, dev, production]
    paths: ['src/**', 'tests/**', '.github/workflows/**']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, dev, production]
  pull_request_target:
    types: [ready_for_review]
```

### Concurrency Management

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

This ensures that only one workflow runs per branch at a time, canceling previous runs when new commits are pushed.

**Sources**: [.github/workflows/lint_and_test.yaml:3-31](), [.github/workflows/release_and_docs.yaml:3-7]()

This document covers advanced usage patterns, external tool integration, and extensibility features in AtomWorks. It provides guidance for users who need to extend the system with custom functionality or integrate with external scientific computing tools.

For basic usage and getting started, see [Overview](#1). For details on the core data processing pipeline, see [atomworks.io - Data Processing](#2). For machine learning pipeline details, see [atomworks.ml - Machine Learning](#3).

## External Tool Integration

AtomWorks provides seamless integration with several external scientific computing libraries, enabling advanced molecular analysis and processing workflows.

### RDKit Integration

AtomWorks offers comprehensive integration with RDKit for small molecule processing and analysis. The integration supports bidirectional conversion between AtomArray objects and RDKit Mol objects.

## RDKit-AtomWorks Integration Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "RDKit Ecosystem"
        A1[Chem.Mol]
        A2[Chem.SDMolSupplier]
        A3[SMILES]
        A4[SDF Files]
        A5[Morgan Fingerprints]
    end
    
    subgraph "AtomWorks RDKit Bridge"
        B1["atom_array_from_rdkit()"]
        B2["smiles_to_rdkit()"]
        B3["sdf_to_rdkit()"]
        B4["fix_mol()"]
        B5["preserve_annotations decorator"]
        B6["get_morgan_fingerprint_from_rdkit_mol()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "AtomWorks Core"
        C1[AtomArray]
        C2[BondList]
        C3[Molecular Annotations]
    end
    
    subgraph "Advanced Features"
        D1["ChEMBLNormalizer"]
        D2["change_metal_bonds_to_dative()"]
        D3["fix_charge_based_on_valence()"]
        D4["RDKIT_BOND_TYPE_TO_BIOTITE mapping"]
    end
    
    A1 --> B1
    A3 --> B2
    A4 --> B3
    B1 --> C1
    B2 --> A1
    B3 --> A1
    A1 --> B6
    B6 --> A5
    
    B4 --> D1
    B4 --> D2
    B4 --> D3
    D4 --> B1
    
    B5 -.-> B1
    B5 -.-> B2
    B5 -.-> B3
    
    C1 --> C2
    C1 --> C3
```

The core conversion functions provide robust molecular data exchange:

- `atom_array_from_rdkit()` converts RDKit Mol objects to AtomArray format, preserving bond information and molecular annotations
- `smiles_to_rdkit()` generates RDKit molecules from SMILES strings with conformer generation
- `sdf_to_rdkit()` loads molecules from SDF files with sanitization options

Advanced molecular processing features include:

- `ChEMBLNormalizer` class for standardizing molecules using ChEMBL pipeline rules
- `fix_mol()` function for automated molecular sanitization and error recovery
- Metal coordination bond handling via `change_metal_bonds_to_dative()`
- Valence-based formal charge correction through `fix_charge_based_on_valence()`

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/tools/rdkit.py:1-766]()

Key enhancements to Biotite functionality:

- Enhanced structure loading via `get_structure()` with improved bond inference and altloc handling
- Universal file reader `read_any()` supporting CIF, BCIF, PDB, and compressed formats
- Automated missing atom placement through template-based reconstruction
- Extended annotation system for chain typing and molecular classification

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/utils/io_utils.py:1-774]()

### File Format Ecosystem

AtomWorks supports a comprehensive range of molecular file formats with automatic type detection and conversion capabilities.

| Format | Extension | Read Support | Write Support | Compression |
|--------|-----------|-------------|---------------|-------------|
| mmCIF | `.cif` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Binary CIF | `.bcif` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| PDB | `.pdb` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| SDF | `.sdf` | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
| FASTA | `.fasta` | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
| MOL | `.mol` | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |

The `infer_pdb_file_type()` function automatically detects file formats, while `parse()` provides a unified interface for all supported formats.

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/utils/io_utils.py:283-318]()

## Extending AtomWorks

AtomWorks is designed for extensibility through its modular transform system and pipeline architecture.

### Transform System Architecture

The transform system provides a standardized interface for data processing operations with built-in validation and composition capabilities.

## Transform System Class Hierarchy

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Base Transform Infrastructure"
        A1["Transform (ABC)"]
        A2["Compose"]
        A3["ApplyFunctionToAtomArray"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Transform Categories"
        B1["Filtering Transforms"]
        B2["Feature Transforms"]
        B3["Encoding Transforms"]
        B4["Geometry Transforms"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Specific Transform Examples"
        C1["RemoveHydrogens"]
        C2["AtomizeByCCDName"] 
        C3["EncodeAtomArray"]
        C4["GetAF3ReferenceMoleculeFeatures"]
        C5["MaskResiduesWithSpecificUnresolvedAtoms"]
        C6["PlaceUnresolvedTokenOnClosestResolvedTokenInSequence"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Validation System"
        D1["check_contains_keys()"]
        D2["check_is_instance()"]
        D3["check_atom_array_annotation()"]
        D4["incompatible_previous_transforms"]
        D5["requires_previous_transforms"]
    end
    
    A1 --> A2
    A1 --> A3
    A1 --> B1
    A1 --> B2
    A1 --> B3
    A1 --> B4
    
    B1 --> C1
    B2 --> C2
    B3 --> C3
    B4 --> C4
    B1 --> C5
    B4 --> C6
    
    A1 --> D1
    A1 --> D2
    A1 --> D3
    C5 --> D4
    C6 --> D5
```

### Custom Transform Development

Creating custom transforms involves implementing the `Transform` abstract base class with proper validation and forward processing logic.

Essential methods for custom transforms:
- `check_input()`: Validates input data structure and required annotations
- `forward()`: Implements the core transformation logic
- Class variables for dependency management: `requires_previous_transforms`, `incompatible_previous_transforms`

Example transform structure pattern:

```python
class CustomTransform(Transform):
    def __init__(self, param1: type, param2: type = default):
        self.param1 = param1
        self.param2 = param2
    
    def check_input(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        check_contains_keys(data, ["atom_array"])
        check_is_instance(data, "atom_array", AtomArray)
        check_atom_array_annotation(data, ["required_annotation"])
    
    def forward(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        # Transform implementation
        return data
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/base.py](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/featurize_unresolved_residues.py:100-144]()

### Pipeline Construction Patterns

AtomWorks supports both declarative and programmatic pipeline construction approaches.

## Pipeline Construction Strategies

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Programmatic Construction"
        A1["Compose([transform1, transform2])"]
        A2["build_af3_transform_pipeline()"]
        A3["build_rf2aa_transform_pipeline()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Declarative Construction" 
        B1["Hydra YAML Configs"]
        B2["_target_: atomworks.ml.transforms.RemoveHydrogens"]
        B3["StructuralDatasetWrapper"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Pipeline Execution"
        C1["Sequential Transform Application"]
        C2["RNG State Management"]
        C3["Error Handling & Recovery"]
        C4["Performance Monitoring"]
    end
    
    A1 --> C1
    A2 --> C1  
    A3 --> C1
    B1 --> B3
    B2 --> B3
    B3 --> C1
    
    C1 --> C2
    C1 --> C3
    C1 --> C4
```

The `Compose` class enables sequential transform chaining with optional RNG state tracking:

```python
pipeline = Compose([
    RemoveHydrogens(),
    AtomizeByCCDName(atomize_by_default=True),
    EncodeAtomArray(encoding=AF3_ATOM37_ENCODING)
], track_rng_state=True)
```

Pre-built pipeline functions like `build_af3_transform_pipeline()` provide model-specific processing workflows with comprehensive parameter configuration.

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py](), [tests/ml/pipelines/test_pipeline_regression.py:27-67]()

## Advanced Usage Patterns

### Caching and Performance Optimization

AtomWorks implements multi-level caching strategies for computational efficiency in large-scale processing workflows.

The `parse()` function supports persistent caching with content-based cache keys:

- Cache key generation via argument hashing: `string_to_md5_hash(args_string, truncate=8)`
- Assembly-aware cache file naming: `{stem}_assembly_{assembly_info}.pkl.gz`
- Selective caching excluding assemblies for space efficiency

Cache directory structure and management:
```
cache_dir/
├── {args_hash}/
│   ├── {structure_id}_assembly_all.pkl.gz
│   ├── {structure_id}_assembly_1.pkl.gz
│   └── ...
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/parser.py:200-257]()

### Error Handling and Recovery

AtomWorks implements robust error handling with graceful degradation strategies:

**Molecular Sanitization Recovery**:
- ChEMBL-style normalization via `ChEMBLNormalizer`
- RDKit standard normalization fallback
- Valence-based charge correction
- Configurable failure modes: `raise_on_failure` parameter

**File Processing Recovery**:
- Automatic format detection with fallback parsing
- Multi-model handling with graceful single-model fallback
- Invalid file error recovery through model selection

**Transform Pipeline Recovery**:
- Transform dependency validation
- Annotation requirement checking
- Graceful handling of missing optional features

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/tools/rdkit.py:266-347](), [src/atomworks/io/utils/io_utils.py:629-647]()

This document covers AtomWorks' integration with external libraries and tools that provide core functionality for biological structure processing, chemical informatics, and machine learning. AtomWorks acts as a bridge between these tools, providing unified interfaces and data conversion utilities.

For information about extending AtomWorks with custom functionality, see [Extending AtomWorks](#6.2). For details on the core data processing pipeline, see [atomworks.io - Data Processing](#2).

## Integration Architecture Overview

AtomWorks integrates with several key external libraries to provide comprehensive biomolecular processing capabilities. The integration follows a layered architecture where external tools provide specialized functionality while AtomWorks provides unified interfaces and seamless data conversion.

## Biotite Integration

Biotite serves as the primary external library for biological structure processing in AtomWorks. All structural data is represented using Biotite's `AtomArray` and `AtomArrayStack` objects, which provide the foundation for AtomWorks' data model.

### Core Data Structures

AtomWorks extensively uses Biotite's structure representations:

- **AtomArray**: Single model atomic structures with annotations
- **AtomArrayStack**: Multi-model structures (e.g., NMR ensembles)
- **BondList**: Bond connectivity information

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "File Formats"
        CIF["CIF Files"]
        PDB["PDB Files"]
        BCIF["Binary CIF"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Biotite I/O"
        CIFFile["pdbx.CIFFile"]
        PDBFile["biotite_pdb.PDBFile"]
        BinaryCIFFile["pdbx.BinaryCIFFile"]
    end
    
    subgraph "AtomWorks Processing"
        GetStructure["get_structure()"]
        ParseAtomArray["parse_atom_array()"]
        AtomArray["AtomArray"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processed Output"
        ParsedData["Parsed Structure Data"]
        Assemblies["Biological Assemblies"]
        Metadata["Structure Metadata"]
    end
    
    CIF --> CIFFile
    PDB --> PDBFile
    BCIF --> BinaryCIFFile
    
    CIFFile --> GetStructure
    PDBFile --> GetStructure
    BinaryCIFFile --> GetStructure
    
    GetStructure --> AtomArray
    AtomArray --> ParseAtomArray
    ParseAtomArray --> ParsedData
    ParsedData --> Assemblies
    ParsedData --> Metadata
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/parser.py:12-18](), [src/atomworks/io/utils/io_utils.py:16-22]()

### Structure Loading and Processing

The `get_structure()` function provides enhanced Biotite integration with additional features for handling bonds and annotations:

```mermaid
graph TD
    FileObj["File Object<br/>(CIFFile/PDBFile)"]
    ExtraFields["extra_fields<br/>Configuration"]
    
    FileObj --> GetStructure["get_structure()"]
    ExtraFields --> GetStructure
    
    GetStructure --> LoadBase["Load Base Structure<br/>pdbx.get_structure()"]
    GetStructure --> AddBonds["_add_bonds()"]
    
    AddBonds --> IntraBonds["Intra-residue Bonds<br/>connect_via_residue_names()"]
    AddBonds --> InterBonds["Inter-residue Bonds<br/>add_inter_residue_bonds()"]
    
    LoadBase --> AtomArrayOutput["AtomArray/AtomArrayStack"]
    IntraBonds --> AtomArrayOutput
    InterBonds --> AtomArrayOutput
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/utils/io_utils.py:180-281](), [src/atomworks/io/utils/io_utils.py:84-177]()

### Bond Handling Integration

AtomWorks extends Biotite's bond handling to correctly process complex biological structures:

- **Intra-residue bonds**: Uses Biotite's CCD-based bond inference
- **Inter-residue bonds**: Custom logic for disulfide bonds, metal coordination, and covalent modifications
- **Bond type correction**: Fixes formal charges and bond orders for inter-residue connections

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/utils/io_utils.py:84-177]()

## RDKit Integration

RDKit provides chemical informatics capabilities for small molecule processing, conformer generation, and molecular standardization. AtomWorks integrates RDKit primarily for ligand and small molecule handling.

### Molecule Conversion Pipeline

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input Sources"
        SMILES["SMILES Strings"]
        SDF["SDF Files"]
        AtomArrayInput["AtomArray<br/>(Small Molecules)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "RDKit Processing"
        SMILESToRDKit["smiles_to_rdkit()"]
        SDFToRDKit["sdf_to_rdkit()"]
        AtomArrayToRDKit["atom_array_to_rdkit()"]
        RDKitMol["rdkit.Chem.Mol"]
    end
    
    subgraph "AtomWorks Output"
        RDKitToAtomArray["atom_array_from_rdkit()"]
        ProcessedAtomArray["AtomArray<br/>(Processed)"]
    end
    
    SMILES --> SMILESToRDKit
    SDF --> SDFToRDKit
    AtomArrayInput --> AtomArrayToRDKit
    
    SMILESToRDKit --> RDKitMol
    SDFToRDKit --> RDKitMol
    AtomArrayToRDKit --> RDKitMol
    
    RDKitMol --> RDKitToAtomArray
    RDKitToAtomArray --> ProcessedAtomArray
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/tools/rdkit.py:390-481](), [src/atomworks/io/tools/rdkit.py:483-632](), [src/atomworks/io/tools/rdkit.py:633-900]()

### Conformer Generation and Standardization

RDKit integration includes sophisticated conformer generation and molecule standardization:

- **Conformer generation**: Uses ETKDG algorithms with UFF minimization
- **ChEMBL standardization**: Implements ChEMBL structure pipeline for molecule normalization
- **Valence correction**: Automatic fixing of formal charges and bond orders

```mermaid
graph TD
    InputMol["Input Molecule"]
    
    InputMol --> FixMol["fix_mol()"]
    FixMol --> ChEMBLNorm["ChEMBL Normalization"]
    FixMol --> RDKitNorm["RDKit Normalization"] 
    FixMol --> ValenceFix["Valence-based Charge Fix"]
    
    ChEMBLNorm --> Sanitized["Sanitized Molecule"]
    RDKitNorm --> Sanitized
    ValenceFix --> Sanitized
    
    Sanitized --> AddHydrogens["Add Hydrogens"]
    AddHydrogens --> ETKDGConf["ETKDG Conformer<br/>Generation"]
    ETKDGConf --> UFFMin["UFF Minimization"]
    UFFMin --> RemoveHydrogens["Remove Hydrogens"]
    RemoveHydrogens --> FinalMol["Final Molecule<br/>with Conformers"]
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/tools/rdkit.py:266-346](), [src/atomworks/io/tools/rdkit.py:390-446]()

### Bond Type Mapping

AtomWorks provides bidirectional conversion between Biotite and RDKit bond representations:

| Biotite BondType | RDKit BondType | Aromatic Flag |
|------------------|----------------|---------------|
| `SINGLE` | `SINGLE` | `False` |
| `DOUBLE` | `DOUBLE` | `False` |
| `TRIPLE` | `TRIPLE` | `False` |
| `AROMATIC_SINGLE` | `SINGLE` | `True` |
| `AROMATIC_DOUBLE` | `DOUBLE` | `True` |

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/tools/rdkit.py:60-97]()

## Integration Patterns and Best Practices

### Data Conversion Patterns

AtomWorks follows consistent patterns for converting between external tool representations:

1. **Preserve Annotations**: Custom decorators maintain metadata during conversions
2. **Error Handling**: Graceful fallbacks when external tools fail
3. **Memory Efficiency**: Lazy loading and streaming for large datasets

```mermaid
graph TD
    ExternalData["External Tool Data"]
    
    ExternalData --> Validate["Validation"]
    Validate --> Convert["Conversion"]
    Convert --> Preserve["Preserve Annotations"]
    Preserve --> ErrorHandle["Error Handling"]
    ErrorHandle --> AtomWorksData["AtomWorks Data"]
    
    ErrorHandle --> Fallback["Fallback Strategy"]
    Fallback --> AtomWorksData
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/tools/rdkit.py:163-196](), [src/atomworks/io/parser.py:254-257]()

### Performance Optimization

- **Caching**: Function-level caching for expensive operations
- **Batch Processing**: Vectorized operations where possible
- **Memory Management**: Explicit cleanup of temporary objects

Sources: [src/atomworks/io/tools/rdkit.py:128-137](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/filters.py:30-43]()

This document provides guidance for developers on creating custom components within the AtomWorks framework. It covers the primary extension points: custom parsers, transforms, dataset wrappers, and token encodings. For information about using existing AtomWorks components, see [Overview](#1). For details on the core processing pipeline, see [atomworks.io - Data Processing](#2) and [atomworks.ml - Machine Learning](#3).

## Extension Architecture Overview

AtomWorks provides several well-defined extension points that allow developers to customize data processing pipelines without modifying core functionality.

**AtomWorks Extension Points Architecture**
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Data Sources"
        PARQUET["metadata.parquet"]
        CIF["Structure Files (.cif)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Extension Points"
        MRP["MetadataRowParser"]
        TF["Transform"]
        DS["BaseDataset"]
        TE["TokenEncoding"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Processing"
        PARSE["atomworks.io.parse()"]
        BUILD_AF3["build_af3_transform_pipeline()"]
        BUILD_RF2AA["build_rf2aa_transform_pipeline()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Concrete Implementations"
        PNPARSER["PNUnitsDFParser"]
        INTERFACEPARSER["InterfacesDFParser"]
        VALIDPARSER["ValidationDFParserLikeAF3"]
        PANDAS_DS["PandasDataset"]
        STRUCT_WRAP["StructuralDatasetWrapper"]
        AF3_ENC["AF3SequenceEncoding"]
        RF2AA_ENC["RF2AA_ATOM36_ENCODING"]
    end
    
    PARQUET --> MRP
    CIF --> PARSE
    MRP --> DS
    PARSE --> TF
    DS --> TF
    TF --> TE
    TF --> BUILD_AF3
    TF --> BUILD_RF2AA
    TE --> BUILD_AF3
    TE --> BUILD_RF2AA
    
    MRP --> PNPARSER
    MRP --> INTERFACEPARSER  
    MRP --> VALIDPARSER
    DS --> PANDAS_DS
    DS --> STRUCT_WRAP
    TE --> AF3_ENC
    TE --> RF2AA_ENC
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/datasets/parsers/base.py:27-85](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/base.py:26-42](), [src/atomworks/ml/datasets/datasets.py:28-59](), [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:254-286](), [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/af3.py:84-133](), [src/atomworks/ml/pipelines/rf2aa.py:154-205]()

## Creating Custom MetadataRowParsers

`MetadataRowParser` subclasses convert dataset rows into a standardized format for the AtomWorks pipeline. The base class defines a required schema and validation framework.

**MetadataRowParser Class Hierarchy**
```mermaid
graph TD
    BASE["MetadataRowParser"]
    BASE --> |"_parse(row)"| IMPL1["AF2FB_DistillationParser"]
    BASE --> |"_parse(row)"| IMPL2["ValidationDFParserLikeAF3"]
    BASE --> |"_parse(row)"| IMPL3["PNUnitsDFParser"]
    BASE --> |"_parse(row)"| CUSTOM["YourCustomParser"]
    
    SCHEMA["Required Schema"] --> BASE
    SCHEMA --> |"example_id: str"| ID
    SCHEMA --> |"path: Path"| PATH
    SCHEMA --> |"extra_info: dict"| EXTRA
```

### Implementation Pattern

Custom parsers must implement the `_parse` method and return a dictionary conforming to the required schema. The base `MetadataRowParser` validates outputs against a predefined schema:

```python
class YourCustomParser(MetadataRowParser):
    def _parse(self, row: pd.Series) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "example_id": row["your_id_column"],
            "path": Path(row["your_path_column"]),
            "assembly_id": "1",  # or row["assembly_column"]
            "extra_info": {
                "custom_field": row.get("custom_data", None),
                "source_metadata": row.to_dict()  # Preserve original row data
            }
        }
```

The `MetadataRowParser.parse()` method automatically validates the output schema and handles common preprocessing like path resolution.

### Required Schema Elements

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `example_id` | `str` | Unique identifier for the example |
| `path` | `Path` | Path to structure file for `atomworks.io.parse` |
| `extra_info` | `dict` | Additional metadata for transforms |

### Parser Examples

The `AF2FB_DistillationParser` demonstrates handling sharded file structures:

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/datasets/parsers/custom_metadata_row_parsers.py:12-95](), [src/atomworks/ml/datasets/parsers/base.py:47-85]()

## Creating Custom Transforms

`Transform` subclasses modify molecular data within processing pipelines. They implement a `forward` method and can include input validation through `check_input`.

**Transform Processing Flow**
```mermaid
graph LR
    INPUT["data: dict"] --> CHECK["check_input()"]
    CHECK --> FORWARD["forward()"]
    FORWARD --> OUTPUT["transformed_data: dict"]
    
    subgraph "Transform Implementation"
        CHECK
        FORWARD
        VALIDATE["Input Validation"]
        PROCESS["Data Processing"]
        CHECK --> VALIDATE
        FORWARD --> PROCESS
    end
```

### Transform Base Pattern

```python
class YourTransform(Transform):
    def __init__(self, your_parameter: float = 1.0):
        self.your_parameter = your_parameter
    
    def check_input(self, data: dict) -> None:
        check_contains_keys(data, ["atom_array", "chain_info"])
        check_is_instance(data, "atom_array", AtomArray)
    
    def forward(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        # Transform the data
        modified_atom_array = self._process_atom_array(data["atom_array"])
        
        # Return modified data
        return {**data, "atom_array": modified_atom_array}
```

### Complex Transform Examples

AtomWorks includes several sophisticated transforms that demonstrate advanced patterns for molecular data processing.

**AddRFTemplates Transform Architecture**
```mermaid
graph TD
    INPUT["AtomArray + chain_info"]
    INPUT --> LOOKUP["_get_rf_template_id()"]
    LOOKUP --> LOAD["_load_rf_template()"]
    LOAD --> RF2AA_TEMPLATE["RF2AATemplate"]
    RF2AA_TEMPLATE --> FILTER["seq_similarity filtering"]
    FILTER --> SUBSET["template.subset()"]
    SUBSET --> CONVERT["template.to_atom_array()"]
    CONVERT --> OUTPUT["data['template']"]
    
    subgraph "External Dependencies"
        LOOKUP --> ENV_LOOKUP["TEMPLATE_LOOKUP_PATH"]
        LOAD --> ENV_BASE["TEMPLATE_BASE_DIR"]
        LOAD --> TORCH_LOAD["torch.load()"]
    end
```

**FeaturizeTemplatesLikeAF3 Transform Flow**
```mermaid
graph LR
    TEMPLATES["data['template']"] --> BLANK["blank_af3_template_features()"]
    BLANK --> FILL["featurize_templates_like_af3()"]
    FILL --> DISTOGRAM["template_distogram calculation"]
    DISTOGRAM --> BACKBONE["template_backbone_frame_mask"]
    BACKBONE --> OUTPUT["data['template_feat']"]
    
    subgraph "Feature Types"
        DISTOGRAM --> BINS["distogram_bins"]
        BACKBONE --> FRAMES["rigid_from_3_points()"]
    end
```

Key patterns in complex transforms:
- Template loading with disk-based caching via `torch.load()`
- Multi-chain processing with `chain_instance_iter()`
- Geometric computations using `rigid_from_3_points()`
- Configurable filtering with sequence similarity thresholds
- Integration with external environment variables for data paths

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/template.py:305-459](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/template.py:700-800](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/dna/pad_dna.py:217-329]()

## Creating Custom Dataset Wrappers

Dataset wrappers provide data loading and processing coordination. AtomWorks offers several base classes for different use cases.

**Dataset Class Hierarchy**
```mermaid
graph TD
    BASE["BaseDataset"]
    BASE --> |"Abstract Methods"| FILE["FileDataset"]
    BASE --> |"Abstract Methods"| PANDAS["PandasDataset"]
    FILE --> STRUCTURAL["StructuralFileDataset"]
    
    WRAPPER["StructuralDatasetWrapper"]
    WRAPPER --> |"Wraps"| FILE
    WRAPPER --> |"Wraps"| PANDAS
    WRAPPER --> |"Wraps"| STRUCTURAL
    
    BASE --> |"__getitem__, __len__"| METHODS
    BASE --> |"id_to_idx, idx_to_id"| INDEXING
    BASE --> |"__contains__"| MEMBERSHIP
```

### Dataset Implementation Requirements

All custom datasets must implement the `BaseDataset` interface. The abstract base class enforces a consistent API across all dataset implementations:

| Method | Purpose | Return Type | Implementation Notes |
|--------|---------|-------------|---------------------|
| `__getitem__(idx)` | Retrieve item by index | `Any` | Must handle integer indices |
| `__len__()` | Dataset size | `int` | Should be fast (cached if needed) |
| `__contains__(example_id)` | Check if ID exists | `bool` | String-based membership test |
| `id_to_idx(example_id)` | Convert ID to index | `int` | Raises `KeyError` if not found |
| `idx_to_id(idx)` | Convert index to ID | `str` | Raises `IndexError` if out of bounds |

The `BaseDataset` provides additional utility methods like `get_example_ids()` which returns all valid example IDs as a list.

### File-Based Dataset Example

`StructuralFileDataset` demonstrates file system integration with automatic ID generation:

```python
class StructuralFileDataset(FileDataset):
    @cached_property
    def data(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        # Generate example IDs from file paths
        example_ids = []
        for file_path in self.file_paths:
            filename = Path(file_path).stem
            while "." in filename:  # Handle .cif.gz
                filename = Path(filename).stem
            example_ids.append(filename)
        
        return pd.DataFrame({
            "path": self.file_paths,
            "example_id": example_ids,
        }).set_index("example_id")
```

### StructuralDatasetWrapper Integration

The `StructuralDatasetWrapper` coordinates parsing, transformation, and error handling:

**StructuralDatasetWrapper Flow**
```mermaid
graph LR
    DATASET["Wrapped Dataset"] --> GETITEM["__getitem__(idx)"]
    GETITEM --> PARSER["MetadataRowParser.parse()"]
    PARSER --> CIF["load_example_from_metadata_row()"]
    CIF --> TRANSFORM["Transform Pipeline"]
    TRANSFORM --> OUTPUT["Processed Data"]
    
    ERROR["Exception Handling"] --> SAVE["save_failed_examples_to_dir"]
    TRANSFORM -.-> ERROR
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/datasets/datasets.py:61-209](), [src/atomworks/ml/datasets/datasets.py:210-359]()

## Creating Custom Token Encodings

`TokenEncoding` defines molecular representations for machine learning models. Custom encodings specify atom mappings and handle unknown residues.

**TokenEncoding Structure**
```mermaid
graph TD
    ENCODING["TokenEncoding"]
    ENCODING --> ATOMS["token_atoms: dict"]
    ENCODING --> UNKNOWN["chemcomp_type_to_unknown: dict"]
    
    ATOMS --> RESIDUES["Residue Tokens"]
    ATOMS --> ATOMNAMES["Atom Names per Token"]
    
    UNKNOWN --> CHEMTYPES["Chemical Component Types"]
    UNKNOWN --> UNKTOKENS["Unknown Token Mappings"]
    
    RESIDUES --> |"'ALA', 'GLY', ..."| STANDARD
    ATOMNAMES --> |"['N', 'CA', 'C', ...]"| POSITIONS
```

### Custom Encoding Pattern

Custom encodings follow the `TokenEncoding` class structure with explicit atom ordering and unknown token handling:

```python
CUSTOM_ENCODING = TokenEncoding(
    token_atoms={
        'YOUR_RES1': ['ATOM1', 'ATOM2', 'ATOM3', ''],
        'YOUR_RES2': ['ATOM1', 'ATOM2', '', ''],
        'UNK': ['', '', '', ''],  # Unknown token
        # Add atom-level tokens for atomized molecules
        6: ['6', '', '', ''],  # Carbon atom
        7: ['7', '', '', ''],  # Nitrogen atom
    },
    chemcomp_type_to_unknown={
        'L-PEPTIDE LINKING': 'UNK',
        'RNA LINKING': 'UNK', 
        'DNA LINKING': 'UNK',
        'NON-POLYMER': 'UNK',
    }
)
```

The `TokenEncoding` class automatically generates lookup dictionaries (`token_to_idx`, `atom_to_idx`) and validation methods (`resolve_unknown_token_name`).

### Encoding Requirements

- All token arrays must have the same length
- Empty positions use empty strings `''`
- Unknown token mappings must reference valid tokens
- Chemical component types must be uppercase

### Built-in Encoding Examples

AtomWorks provides several standard encodings for different model architectures:

| Encoding | Atoms per Token | Total Tokens | Use Case |
|----------|----------------|--------------|----------|
| `AF2_ATOM14_ENCODING` | 14 | 21 | AlphaFold2-style protein modeling |
| `AF2_ATOM37_ENCODING` | 37 | 21 | Extended protein atom representation |
| `RF2AA_ATOM36_ENCODING` | 36 | 89 | RoseTTAFold2AA with proteins + nucleic acids |
| `LEGACY_RF2_ATOM14_ENCODING` | 14 | 21 | Legacy RF template compatibility |

**AF3SequenceEncoding Pattern**
```mermaid
graph LR
    AF3_SEQ["AF3SequenceEncoding"] --> RESIDUES["all_res_names"]
    AF3_SEQ --> SPECIAL["special_tokens: <G>, <M>, UNK"]
    RESIDUES --> AA["is_aa_like: 20 standard + variants"]
    RESIDUES --> RNA["is_rna_like: A,U,G,C + mods"]
    RESIDUES --> DNA["is_dna_like: DA,DT,DG,DC + mods"]
    SPECIAL --> GAP["<G>: gap token"]
    SPECIAL --> MASK["<M>: mask token"]
    SPECIAL --> UNK_TOK["UNK: unknown residue"]
```

The `AF3SequenceEncoding` class extends basic encodings with biochemical classification methods and one-hot encoding support.

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:36-251](), [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:254-286](), [src/atomworks/ml/encoding_definitions.py:289-318]()

## Testing Custom Extensions

AtomWorks provides testing utilities and patterns for validating custom components.

### Parser Testing

```python
def test_your_custom_parser():
    parser = YourCustomParser()
    sample_row = pd.Series({
        'your_id_column': 'test_id',
        'your_path_column': '/path/to/file.cif'
    })
    
    result = parser.parse(sample_row)
    
    assert result['example_id'] == 'test_id'
    assert isinstance(result['path'], Path)
    assert isinstance(result['extra_info'], dict)
```

### Transform Testing

```python
def test_your_transform():
    from atomworks.ml.utils.testing import cached_parse
    
    # Load test data
    data = cached_parse("test_structure.cif")
    
    # Apply transform
    transform = YourTransform(your_parameter=2.0)
    result = transform(data)
    
    # Validate output
    assert "atom_array" in result
    assert len(result["atom_array"]) > 0
```

### Integration Testing

AtomWorks provides comprehensive test fixtures for pipeline validation. Use the fixtures from `tests/ml/conftest.py` for end-to-end testing:

**Test Infrastructure**
```mermaid
graph TD
    FIXTURES["conftest.py fixtures"]
    FIXTURES --> DATASETS["Dataset fixtures"]
    FIXTURES --> PIPELINES["Pipeline fixtures"]
    
    DATASETS --> PN_UNITS["pn_units_pandas_dataset"]
    DATASETS --> INTERFACES["interfaces_pandas_dataset"]
    DATASETS --> VALIDATION["validation_pandas_dataset"]
    
    PIPELINES --> AF3_PN["af3_pn_units_dataset"]
    PIPELINES --> RF2AA_PN["rf2aa_pn_units_dataset"]
    PIPELINES --> AF3_VALID["af3_validation_dataset"]
    
    TEST_CONSTANTS --> MSA_DIRS["PROTEIN_MSA_DIRS, RNA_MSA_DIRS"]
    TEST_CONSTANTS --> TEMPLATE_DIRS["TEMPLATE_DIR, TEMPLATE_LOOKUP"]
```

Example integration test using fixtures:

```python
def test_custom_pipeline_integration(af3_pn_units_dataset):
    """Test custom components with real AF3 pipeline"""
    # Get first example
    example = af3_pn_units_dataset[0]
    
    # Validate pipeline output structure
    assert "feats" in example
    assert "ground_truth" in example
    assert "example_id" in example
    
    # Test custom transform integration
    custom_transform = YourCustomTransform()
    modified_data = custom_transform(example)
    assert "your_custom_field" in modified_data
```

## Integration Patterns

### Pipeline Integration

Custom components integrate into AtomWorks pipelines through the `Compose` transform and `StructuralDatasetWrapper`:

**Custom Pipeline Integration**
```mermaid
graph LR
    CONFIG["Hydra Config"] --> BUILD["build_*_transform_pipeline()"]
    BUILD --> COMPOSE["Compose([transforms])"]
    COMPOSE --> CUSTOM["YourCustomTransform"]
    COMPOSE --> BUILTIN["Built-in Transforms"]
    
    WRAPPER["StructuralDatasetWrapper"] --> PARSER["YourCustomParser"]
    WRAPPER --> DATASET["BaseDataset"]
    WRAPPER --> TRANSFORM["Transform Pipeline"]
    
    DATASET --> GETITEM["__getitem__()"]
    GETITEM --> PARSER
    PARSER --> CIF_PARSE["cached_parse()"]
    CIF_PARSE --> TRANSFORM
```

Example integration with AF3 pipeline:

```python
def build_custom_af3_pipeline(**kwargs):
    """Custom AF3 pipeline with your extensions"""
    return Compose([
        # Early processing
        RemoveHydrogens(),
        YourCustomStructureValidator(),
        
        # Standard AF3 transforms
        AddGlobalAtomIdAnnotation(),
        AtomizeByCCDName(atomize_by_default=True),
        
        # Your custom processing
        YourCustomFeatureExtractor(param=1.0),
        
        # Continue with AF3 pipeline...
    ])

# Integration with StructuralDatasetWrapper
dataset = StructuralDatasetWrapper(
    dataset=your_pandas_dataset,
    dataset_parser=YourCustomParser(),
    transform=build_custom_af3_pipeline(**config),
    cif_parser_args={"cache_dir": cache_dir}
)
```

### Executable Integration

For transforms requiring external tools, AtomWorks provides the `Executable` base class following the `X3DNAFiber` pattern:

**Executable Integration Architecture**
```mermaid
graph TD
    TRANSFORM["YourTransform"] --> EXEC_CALL["YourExecutable().run()"]
    EXEC_CALL --> EXEC_CLASS["YourExecutable(Executable)"]
    
    EXEC_CLASS --> SETUP["_setup()"]
    EXEC_CLASS --> BINPATH["get_bin_path()"]
    EXEC_CLASS --> VERSION["get_version()"]
    EXEC_CLASS --> RUN["run()"]
    
    SETUP --> ENV_VAR["Environment Variables"]
    SETUP --> CONFIG_FILE["Configuration Files"]
    BINPATH --> PATH_RESOLUTION["Path Resolution Logic"]
    RUN --> SUBPROCESS["subprocess.run()"]
    RUN --> VALIDATION["Output Validation"]
```

Example executable integration:

```python
class YourExecutable(Executable):
    def _setup(self) -> None:
        """Validate executable availability"""
        if not self.get_bin_path():
            raise ExecutableNotFoundError("your_tool not found")
    
    def get_bin_path(self) -> Path | None:
        """Get path to executable binary"""
        return self._find_executable("your_tool")
    
    def run(self, input_data: dict) -> dict:
        """Execute external tool"""
        cmd = [str(self.get_bin_path()), "--input", input_data["file"]]
        result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return {"output": result.stdout, "success": result.returncode == 0}
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/executables/x3dna.py:10-63](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/dna/pad_dna.py:570-618]()

### Error Handling

Implement comprehensive error handling for production use:

```python
class YourTransform(Transform):
    def forward(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        try:
            return self._process_data(data)
        except YourSpecificError as e:
            logger.warning(f"Transform failed: {e}")
            return data  # Return unmodified data
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Unexpected error: {e}")
            raise
```

Sources: [src/atomworks/ml/executables/x3dna.py:10-63](), [src/atomworks/ml/datasets/datasets.py:308-327](), [src/atomworks/ml/transforms/dna/pad_dna.py:570-618]()
